# JOURNEY.md

<!-- The structural and temporal design spec. Pairs with DESIGN.md (visual tokens). For visual tokens, see DESIGN.md (created in Phase 2 of the Stage 1 plan; it does not exist yet). -->

**Product:** Kiwi (`kiwi-ui`) · **Plan:** Kiwi UI refresh, Stage 1 (visual and verbal layer) · **Phase:** 1, as-is Discover · **Written:** 2026-10-16 · **Base commit:** `ef65c1d` on `feature/kiwi-ui-stage-1-design`

This file records the interface **as it is today**. Stage 1 changes colour, type, density, the mascot and the words. It does not move page regions, add routes, change navigation or change flows, so nothing here is redesigned: every section describes, and the one forward-looking column, *Fix* in the Defect register's summary, names a direction and an owning phase, not a design. Later phases append to it (mascot placements, revised microcopy and the revision index, chart and table specs) and leave the as-is record intact. Phase 4's mascot placements are the `Companion (Phase 4)` bullet on each affected entry (SR-1, SR-5, SR-6, S-01, S-05, S-06, S-08, S-10, A-01, A-02, A-13, A-19), each naming the `companion.slot.*` token, the size from `md` and below it, the pose and the backing; the state machine itself is `kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Companion`. Phase 5's words are the `Copy (Phase 5)` bullet on each entry (old → new, the rules, a one-line rationale) and the `## Revision index` (every changed string with its anchor, rules and the tests that mention it); the voice, the rules, the vocabulary and the shared strings are in `kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Voice and tone`.

## Reading guide

**Sources.** Brief: `.design-foundations/research/2026-10-16-kiwi-ui-visual-refresh.md` (G1-G15, Appendix A). Tour: `.design-foundations/research/2026-10-16-kiwi-ui-tour.md`. Code: `kiwi-ui/src/` at the base commit, read-only.

**Evidence markers.**

| Marker | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[T]` | Observed live in the 2026-10-16 tour (student side at 1440 wide, admin side at about 960 wide, older backend, one demo class, default states). |
| `[S]` | Taken from source only. **Not observed live**, except where `[L]` says so. Every error state, empty state, role variant and dialog is `[S]` unless the tour or a live check says otherwise. |
| `[L]` | Checked live by the coordinator on 2026-10-16, after the tour, on the dev server with an admin account: the course list (S-01) with its view-switch icon and class card, the Experiment toggle row on a student class page, and a typed app URL (R-5). It is not part of the tour, so it is not `[T]`. |
| `` `src/pages/Courses.tsx:11` `` | Code anchor, path relative to `kiwi-ui/`, line number at the base commit. Every claim about code behaviour has one. |
| `TD-nn` | A finding from the tour, in the [Defect register](#defect-register). |
| `SF-nn` | Found in source and not in the tour. Recorded for later phases; kept apart from `TD-` so DW-1.5 stays auditable. |
| `m:<id>` | The matrix state that a States bullet or an overlay item describes, for example `m:loaded` or `m:ov:edit-dialog`. The [Verification matrix](#verification-matrix) is generated from these ids (see [How an entry is organised](#how-an-entry-is-organised)). |
| "string" | A UI string quoted verbatim from source. Capitals are noted where they come from CSS rather than the string. |

**Severity** (Nielsen 0-4: 0 not a problem, 1 cosmetic, 2 minor, 3 major, 4 catastrophe) is frequency x impact x persistence. It is a single-evaluator rating from tour notes and source, so it finds *likely* problems, not real frequency, and should be re-rated against user data in Stage 2. Contrast and legibility findings are filed under heuristic 4 (Consistency and standards, with WCAG AA as the standard; the brief names no version, and 2.2 is assumed) because Nielsen's ten name neither. A contrast row cites its WCAG 2.2 success criterion beside the heuristic: SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) for text, SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast for icons, borders and chart marks.

**Roles.** S student (`systemRole` `user`), I instructor, A admin (`systemRole` `admin` or `isAdmin`), "signed out". Role information has three layers and each entry keeps them apart: *Appendix A* (the brief's intent), *entry visibility* (which roles are shown a sidebar or menu entry, `[S]`), and the *guard* (what the frontend route wrappers in `src/auth/` actually admit). The [Verification matrix](#verification-matrix) follows Appendix A as the user updated it on 2026-10-16, the intended access model: a role gets a verified row if and only if Appendix A grants it, and a role that today's guards let in but Appendix A does not grant gets a record-only defect row. Every page was walked once per role in source against today's guards; none was run. The outcomes are in the [Role outcomes](#role-outcomes).

**Links deferred to Phase 2.** DESIGN.md does not exist yet, so the cross-links the journey template asks for are written when Phase 2 creates it: in DESIGN.md, "For IA and flow spec, see JOURNEY.md"; in `kiwi-ui/CLAUDE.md`, a `## Design Context` block with `- **Journey spec**: JOURNEY.md` (that file has no such block today). The repository-root `JOURNEY.md` link is the orchestrator's setup step after Phase 1.

---

## Job

**Deferred to Stage 2.**

Why:

- Stage 1 changes no flows, so a job story would not change a single Stage 1 decision. The brief says so directly: "Jobs-to-be-done and journeys are Stage 2 inputs" (brief, *Who*).
- A job story is research output, not a drafting exercise. The method the journey doctrine recommends, the Switch interview (Moesta: push, pull, anxiety, habit), needs interviews with real users of Kiwi. None has been run and no JTBD school has been chosen for the project. A story written now would be a hypothesis presented as a finding, and could not rule out any product decision (journey-caveats, *JTBD school-mixing* and the circular-statement warning).
- The audiences are named in the brief and listed here as context only, not as jobs: students; instructors and admins; Kiwi App developers; researchers running chat experiments.

Stage 2 needs: one JTBD school picked for the whole project, interviews per audience, and a named owner.

## Journey

**Deferred to Stage 2.** No journey map, swim lane or emotion curve is drawn in this file.

Why:

- A journey map is an organisational change tool and needs a **named owner**, a **research basis** (interviews, diary study, analytics or support-call analysis) and an **update cadence**. This project has none of the three. A map drawn from a tour and a code read would be journey-map theatre: 83% of CX professionals report that their maps do not drive change (Watermark Consulting 2023), and an emotion curve drawn without research is the commonest sign of it (NN/g, Gibbons 2018).
- The tour is a current-state page review of two accounts at two viewports. It records what pages look like, not what users tried to do or felt while doing it.

Research basis: **UNGROUNDED**. Owner: none assigned. Review cadence: none.

## IA

**Validation and any redesign: deferred to Stage 2.** What follows is the current route map recorded as-is and **UNVALIDATED**. A sitemap is not an information architecture (Rosenfeld/Morville): a tidy tree can encode the wrong mental model, and neither a card sort (to test grouping and labels) nor a tree test (to test the structure) has been run. Nothing below asserts that the structure or the labels match how users think.

Why deferred: Stage 1 may not move or resize page regions, add or remove navigation items, or add routes (brief, *Stage 1 boundary*), and IA validation can recommend exactly those changes.

### Observed, not chosen

- **Organisation scheme:** audience first (student area, auth area, admin area), then inside admin *system scope* (sidebar) versus *class scope* (class sub-menu). Observed, not validated.
- **Structure:** student side is a hub (course list) feeding a class workspace with tabs; admin side is a tree (sidebar, then a class sub-menu under "Classes" or "My Classes"). `SR-2`, `SR-3`.
- **Global navigation:** the top bar (`SR-1`): logo, class switcher, a view switch for instructors and admins, logout.
- **Local navigation:** the student class tab bar (`SR-2`); the admin sidebar and class sub-menu (`SR-3`); the admin page header's back button (`SR-4`).
- **Contextual navigation:** class cards on the course list (S-01); navigation actions returned by the AI tutor (`src/components/GlobalChat/GlobalChatModal.tsx:69-95`).
- **Breadcrumbs:** none. **Search:** a class finder in the class switcher, plus per-page searches.
- **Labelling:** sidebar labels and page headings disagree in four pairs (TD-21); instructors see "My Classes" where admins see "Classes" (`src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:464`).

**Validation: NOT VALIDATED.** No card sort. No tree test.

## Flows

**Deferred to Stage 2.** No user flow or task flow is drawn.

Why: Stage 1 does not change flows (brief, *Stage 1 boundary*: "changing flows" is out), so a diagram would document nothing Stage 1 touches and would invite changes it may not make. Flows are better drawn once Job and Journey have a research basis.

As-is fragments the page specs already carry (pointers, not diagrams):

- **Sign-in and role redirect:** S-05, S-07, `UnprotectedRoute`; instructors and admins land on `/admin`, everyone else on `/` (`src/pages/Login.tsx:72-78`).
- **Consent gate:** `ProtectedRoute` to S-09 and back to `/`, only when a consent form URL is configured (`src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:55-58`).
- **Session expiry and B2:** a second 401 clears the session and goes to `/login?timeout=true` (`src/utils/middleware.ts:61-102`), shown as a banner on S-05.
- **MCP OAuth round trip:** SR-6 and A-07 store a return context, leave for the provider, and `ProtectedRoute` replays it (`src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:17-44`). See SF-03 for the student-side return path.

## Page specs

34 page entries (`S-01`-`S-10` student, auth and fallback; `A-01`-`A-24` admin), preceded by the seven shared regions (`SR-1`-`SR-7`) that the pages sit inside and followed by the redirect rows (`R-1`-`R-5`). Order follows the route map in [IA](#ia). Four components serve several routes and are specified once, with every route in the heading: `ClassEdit` (A-13), `AdminAppPage` (A-12, three routes), `ExperimentForm` (A-20), `AnnotateDocument` (A-24).

### How an entry is organised

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Source | The page component and the children that were read, with anchors. |
| Roles (Appendix A) | Exactly as the brief's Appendix A records them (S, I, A). |
| Guard (code) | What the frontend wrapper admits. Where it differs from Appendix A the entry says so and cites a discrepancy `D-n` from [Role discrepancies](#role-discrepancies). |
| Entry visibility | Which roles are *shown* a sidebar or menu entry, where that differs from the guard. A third layer between intent and guard; `[S]`. |
| Density | One value per page, set by the route area: **comfortable** for student and auth routes, **compact** for `/admin/*` (brief, *Density*). |
| Density overrides | Reading surfaces (chat answers, PDF pages, materials) are comfortable even inside a compact page; tool chrome (IDE, PDF and table toolbars) is compact even inside a comfortable page. Listed as found; Phase 3 fixes the boundary. |
| Paper surfaces (G5) | PDF pages, templated-email previews and Kiwi App iframes: their *content* stays light in dark mode, their frames and toolbars follow the mode. User-uploaded images and Python/R plots are listed apart as "never recoloured" (G5 keeps them outside "paper"). |
| Purpose, Entry points, Content blocks, States, Primary CTA, Exit / next | The journey page-spec format. |
| State ids (`m:<id>`) | Each States bullet starts with the id of the matrix state it describes, written as a code span such as `m:loaded` or `m:ov:edit-dialog`; each overlay item carries its id. `m:none` marks a bullet that is deliberately not a matrix state (the state is absent, or it is a component state), `m:to:X` a hand-over to another page or region, `m:G-n` a bullet covered by mechanism row G-n of the [Role outcomes](#role-outcomes), and `@S,I,A` after an id limits it to those roles. A "Page-specific" bullet is a note and needs no id, unless it also describes a state, in which case it carries one. The [Verification matrix](#verification-matrix) is generated from these ids. |
| Stage 1 hooks | Where the brief's allowed element changes land (mascot avatar and composer peek, empty-state illustrations, class-card fallback, not-found content, Display-menu button). Existing surfaces only, not designs. |
| Tour defects (in boundary) | `TD-nn (heuristic, severity)` from the [Defect register](#defect-register). `TD-C1` (the Material Design 2014 purple palette) applies to every entry and is listed first in each. |
| Source-found | `SF-nn`: seen in code and not in the tour. |
| Not observed live | States and variants known from source only. |

### Role discrepancies

The matrix follows Appendix A as the user updated it on 2026-10-16 (the intended access model). These are the places where Appendix A, the entry-visibility layer and today's guards do not agree. Each is a defect and none is designed around; by the one rule a role that Appendix A does not grant gets a record-only defect row, never a supported row.

| ID | Discrepancy | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 | Appendix A marks A-04, A-05, A-07 and A-08 "A (admin-only)", and the user's decision of 2026-10-16 keeps every system-level page admin-only for instructors. `AdminProtectedRoute` admits `isAdmin === true` **or** `systemRole === 'instructor'`, so instructors pass it. Behind the wrapper the backend refuses an instructor on the first request (`AdminGuard` or `ProfGuard`, 401), so today an instructor sees the first frame and is signed out (B2); the intended outcome is a no-permission state (D-8). By the one rule the instructor rows of these four pages are record-only defect rows, not supported rows. | `src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:40`; `src/App.tsx:140-159`; [Instructors on admin-only pages](#instructors-on-admin-only-pages-d-8) |
| D-2 | Appendix A marks `/login`, `/register`, `/auth/callback` "all". `UnprotectedRoute` admits signed-out users only; a signed-in user (both `authToken` and `user` present) is redirected to `/admin` (instructor, admin) or `/`; with only one of the two present the page renders. | `src/auth/UnprotectedRoute.tsx:19-26` |
| D-3 | Appendix A marks `/authorize` "per route guard". There is no wrapper. | `src/App.tsx:84-87` |
| D-4 | Entry visibility against Appendix A. The system sidebar entries are admin-only for instructors, as the decision wants (`AdminLayout.tsx:50-110`). In the class sub-menu three entries are hidden from instructors although Appendix A grants them: Enroll Students (A-16) and Class Email (A-17), for the instructors of the class, and Class Apps (A-23). Class Flags (A-15) and Class MCP & Tools (A-22) are hidden and admin-only, as intended; Materials (A-14) and Class Analytics (A-18) need a per-class instructor permission. Entry visibility is not a guard: an instructor can still open every URL (D-8). | `src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:50-110`; `src/pages/admin/ClassLayout.tsx:36-44,148-166`; SR-3 |
| D-5 (B1, B2) | The brief says `/admin` admits admins and instructors, and the intended model is that students cannot enter it. The `/admin` layout is wrapped in `ProtectedRoute` only, so any signed-in user reaches the shell (B1). What a student gets today depends on the page: 5 render (A-01, A-02, A-12, A-18, A-23), 2 raise an `alert()` (A-14, A-24), 5 redirect (A-03, A-04, A-05, A-07, A-08) and 12 end in B2, where the first request is refused with 401 and the middleware signs the user out as "session expired". These outcomes are recorded in [Students on `/admin/*`](#students-on-admin-b1), not as rows. | `src/App.tsx:129-135`; tour B1, B2; `src/utils/middleware.ts:61-102` |
| D-6 | The OAuth-return handler sends students to `/class/{classId}` and `/class/{classId}/pdf/{pdfId}`. Neither is in the route table (the class route is `/:classID`), so both land on S-10. | `src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:31-35` vs `src/App.tsx:112-124` |
| D-7 | Appendix A makes A-03 (`/admin/analytics`) admin-only. The page redirects a non-admin to `/admin/classes` after its first render, while its data requests start anyway and are refused with 403 (two `alert()`s for a student, one for an instructor). The turn-away is intended; its form is the defect: an instructor should see a no-permission state (D-8), not an `alert()` and a bounce. | `src/pages/admin/Analytics.tsx:241-252`; [Instructors on admin-only pages](#instructors-on-admin-only-pages-d-8) |
| D-8 | Appendix A makes 12 admin pages admin-only for instructors: A-02 (New class) to A-11, and inside a class A-15 and A-22. An instructor who reaches one should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. That state does not exist today. Instead the guards let the instructor in and the backend refuses the first request with 401, which the front end treats as an expired session (B2) on 10 of the pages; A-03 raises an `alert()` and redirects (D-7); on A-02 the form renders and the submit is refused (B2); `AdminProtectedRoute` admits instructors on four of them (D-1). The chat agent's sitemap even offers A-02 and A-03 to instructors (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:60-70`). Register: B4. | `../kiwi/src/auth/auth.guard.ts:53-133`; `src/utils/middleware.ts:61-102`; [Instructors on admin-only pages](#instructors-on-admin-only-pages-d-8) |
| D-9 | Appendix A grants Enrolment (A-16) and Class email (A-17) to the instructors of the class. `ProfGuard` needs a `professor` enrolment, and assigning an instructor creates none, so the backend refuses the instructors of the class (401) and the front end signs them out (B2). Their rows stay verified rows; the refusal is the defect. Register: B5; SF-65. | `../kiwi/src/auth/auth.guard.ts:84-133`; `../kiwi/src/instructor-class/instructor-class.service.ts:14-62` |

### Rules used in every entry

- **Density.** Student and auth route areas: comfortable. `/admin/*`: compact. Reading surfaces (chat answers, PDF pages, materials): comfortable everywhere. Tool chrome (IDE toolbar, PDF toolbar, table toolbars): compact everywhere.
- **Paper (G5).** PDF pages and templated-email previews stay light in dark mode (fidelity); Kiwi App iframes stay light (no theme channel reaches them, `kiwi-app-sdk/src/types.ts`). Code editors, code blocks, output consoles and every Kiwi-drawn surface follow the mode and are **not** paper.
- **Primary CTA** is the page's single filled action. Where a view region shows several filled buttons the entry lists them all: the brief allows at most one filled primary per view region.

**Shared regions.** Regions that appear on many routes are specified once here and referenced from the page entries.

It opens a popover with a search field "Find class…" (`:219`, accessible name "Search classes" `:222`), a listbox "Classes" (`:257`) whose selected row carries a check mark, and for admins a footer action "Create New Class" (`src/constants/classCopy.ts:1`, `ClassSwitcher.tsx:388`) that opens `/admin/new-class` (`TopNav.tsx:185-187`).

- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default: student bar = logo, class switcher (on class routes), logout `[T]`; admin bar adds the view switch `[T]`.
  - `m:loading` Loading: class-name skeleton (`TopNav.tsx:169-175`); the class list shows "Loading classes…" with a spinner (`ClassSwitcher.tsx:269-280`). `[S]`

  - `m:ov:class-switcher` Switcher open `[S]`: the popover of block 4, with its search field, its "Classes" listbox and, for admins, the footer action.
  - `m:none` Error: none shown. A failed class-list fetch leaves an empty list and logs to the console (`AdminLayout.tsx:363-365`; `src/pages/ClassLayout.tsx:177-179`). `[S]`

- **Primary CTA:** none (navigation chrome).
- **Exit / next:** logo to `/` or `/admin`; switcher to `/:classID…` or `/admin/class/:classID…`; view switch; Logout to R-3.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the Display-menu button (brief G4) joins the right-hand icon group, next to Logout. G2 (neutral institution logo) applies to block 2; the mascot mark is what block 2 already shows when no institution is configured.
- **Companion (Phase 4):** no companion placement here. Block 2's fallback mark stays the P2 app tile (`kiwi-mark.svg`, as today; G2 lets Kiwi's own marks keep the brand palette); it is not a companion state and never animates. - **Companion (Phase 4):** (1) **Tutor avatar**, `companion.slot.avatar` 32 px on every tutor row (12 px gap to the answer column), on the `--companion-backing` disc in dark mode; only the newest tutor message's avatar animates, through the seven avatar states of `DESIGN.md § Companion` (`walk` while waiting or while a tool runs before any text, the shallow `speaking` dip while text streams, one `hop` of about 1.2 s at completion, a `wave` on Thumbs up, the `error` pose on the error row, `offline` asleep, the `idle` still otherwise); older rows and the welcome row hold the idle still; in experiment compare mode only the avatar of the most recently started answer animates (ties: column A), the other column holds stills. (2) **Composer peek**: `peek` and `retract` belong to the composer, not the avatar. `companion.slot.peek` 48 px anchored to the composer field's top-right corner: its right edge on the field's right edge and its bottom edge on the field's top edge, inside the 48 px lane formed by the message region's 24 px bottom padding and the composer's 24 px top padding (raised from 12 px for the lane). It shows once per focus session, at the first keystroke after the student focused the composer by pointer or keyboard (the focus the app hands back after an answer starts no session), only while the message region is at scroll end (so it never overlaps text) and the newest avatar is still; it retracts 1.5 s after the last keystroke or on blur, reversing from the current drawing; it is cut, with no retract, on send (`walk` has priority) and when the slash-command menu opens in its lane; it is absent whenever motion is off at any level. (3) **Empty conversation**: the welcome row renders as the empty-state frame's inline variant, `companion.slot.inline` 64 px idle still above the welcome line. (4) **Launcher**: the locked 56 px `--accent-solid` disc carries the companion's portrait silhouette with a filled speech bubble (`launcher-glyph.svg`, `companion.slot.launcher` 28 px, `--accent-on-solid`); it never animates. (5) **Announcements**: the error row is `role="alert"` (its subtypes: retryable with Retry; quota or permission with a diagnosis and no Retry; backend error text delivered as a bubble, classed `error`, never a hop); the composer's offline line takes the lock's warning status form (`--status-warning-surface`, `--status-warning-text`, the triangle icon: offline is a condition, not an error) with `role="status"`, set once after the 2 s hysteresis (Stop stays enabled while an answer was pending; the field is disabled with the offline reason; the pending tutor row shows static text, "Paused while you're offline" (final, Phase 5), never the in-progress dots); completion is announced once by a polite live region ("Kiwi finished answering."), after which focus moves to the composer, which announces only its own name; a like is a polite live region ("Feedback saved.") plus the pressed thumb. Sizes are the same at 390 px (the panel is fullscreen). Signals the state machine needs beyond those listed above: a per-focus-session typing flag with a 1.5 s expiry, `isStreaming`, online status with 2 s hysteresis, a user-abort flag, scroll-end detection on the message region (implementation plan). Every mascot element is `aria-hidden`; the text twins are in the state table.
- **Companion (amended 2026-10-18):** the tutor avatar draws full-body drawings only, in one framing for every state (`DESIGN.md § Companion`, `§ Lock amendments`). It runs from the send until the answer is complete, through the wait, the tool steps and the streaming text, with no restart at the first token, then hops and flies once (about 1.2 s) and stands on the standing still, the drawing the hop lands on; a like plays the same `wave`; error and offline rest on the standing still while their rows carry the state. In the bullet above this supersedes the shallow `speaking` dip, the `error` pose, `offline` asleep and the portrait idle still for the avatar; older rows, the welcome row and the welcome frame (64 px) hold the standing still. The composer peek, the launcher, the sizes, one mover and the announcements are unchanged, and the page placements on the other pages keep their stills on purpose.

### SR-7 · Experiment Assistant (floating panel)

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/experiments/ExperimentAssistant.tsx:144-680`. Mounted by A-19 (`ExperimentList.tsx:241`), A-20 (`ExperimentForm.tsx:1241`) and A-21 (`ExperimentDetail.tsx:426`); each page has its own instance and module-level variables carry state between them (`ExperimentAssistant.tsx:121-133`).
- **Appears on:** A-19 in every state; A-20 except while an edit load shows its spinner (`ExperimentForm.tsx:607-612`); A-21 except during its spinner and not-found returns, and the spinner returns after every Activate, Re-activate or Turn off (`ExperimentDetail.tsx:93-95,127-134,156-163`).
- **Roles / Guard:** inherits the host page; no role gate inside (B1, D-5). **Density:** compact. **Paper surfaces:** none.
- **Opening rule:** `useState(() => persistedOpen ?? /\/experiments\/?$/.test(location.pathname))` (`ExperimentAssistant.tsx:167-169`). With no earlier state this session the panel starts **open on the list page** (path ends in `/experiments`) and as a launcher on the form and detail pages; afterwards the last open or closed state is reused. It resets when the class changes or on a full reload (`:129,153-161,188-190`). A draft reply does not open it; it navigates to A-20 (`:221-230`).
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Launcher (closed) `m:launcher`: a 56 px circular button, aria-label "open experiment assistant", white with a 2 px `#6a1b9a` border, a sparkle icon (`AutoAwesomeOutlined`) and a violet shadow, `z-index` 1250, draggable, no tooltip or visible text — `:411-454`.
  2. Panel (open) `m:panel-open`: MUI `Paper`, elevation 12, fixed, `z-index` 1250, 390 x 560 by default, clamped to the viewport, minimum 320 x 360; non-modal (no backdrop, no focus trap, no `role`), so the page behind stays usable — `:55-58,76-105,457-482`. Derived at 1440 x 900 with the sidebar open: panel x 794-1184, y 316-876, which covers the main content right of centre. It sits above the top bar (1000) and the Kiwi Chat launcher (1200) and below the Kiwi Chat panel (modal, 1300) (`TopNav.tsx:88`; `GlobalChatButton.tsx:239`; `GlobalChatModal.tsx:149`).
  3. Header, the drag handle: `linear-gradient(135deg, #6a1b9a 0%, #616161 100%)` with white text, an avatar with a sparkle icon, title "Experiment Assistant", caption "Describe it · I'll draft the config", and a white close icon with no accessible name — `:484-517`; `experimentUi.tsx:35-37`.
  4. Message area on a faint violet tint, auto-scrolling; empty state: a 56 px circle with a sparkle icon and "Describe the experiment you want — e.g. "Two groups 50/50: control on openai with default prompts, treatment on qwen that never gives direct answers." I'll draft the config and open it for review." — `:520-548`.
  5. Bubbles: plain `pre-wrap` text, 14 px, no markdown, no names or timestamps; user bubbles on the violet gradient, assistant bubbles white with a violet hairline — `:549-576`. A three-dot typing indicator while waiting (`:577-581`). After a draft, a text button `m:draft-json` "View last draft JSON" / "Hide last draft JSON" revealing a `<pre>` of the config (`:585-614`).
  6. Composer: multiline field with placeholder "Describe your experiment…", Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line; a 40 px send icon button on the gradient with no accessible name — `:616-648`.
  7. Resize grip, aria-label "resize experiment assistant" — `:649-672`.
- **States:**
  - `m:waiting` Loading `[S]`: the typing indicator; Send disabled; no stop or cancel (`:386`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: block 4.
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: an assistant-style bubble "⚠️ {e.message}", which stays in the history and is sent with the next request; no retry (`:387-402`). A server-side failure because the chat model is not configured arrives as an ordinary reply: "The design assistant is unavailable — the server's chat model isn't configured. Set LLM_API_KEY (or QWEN_API_KEY) in the backend .env and restart, then try again." (`../kiwi/src/experiment/experiment.service.ts:107-115`): developer-facing text.
  - `m:reply` `m:to:A-20` Success `[S]`: the reply is shown unmodified, possibly with a fenced JSON block as plain text; a valid config makes the panel navigate to A-20 with no toast (`:396-397`).
  - Page-specific `[S]`: conversation, input and positions persist across experiment pages; switching class clears messages (`:153-161`); no control to clear the conversation; the close icon is the only way to hide the panel (no Escape, no click-away, `:514`).
- **Primary CTA:** the unlabelled Send icon button → posts the whole conversation and, if the reply holds a config, opens A-20 prefilled (`:385-406,634-647`). There is no labelled filled button.
- **Exit / next:** close icon → launcher at its saved position; a draft → A-20.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** none allowed here; the panel is a second AI surface beside SR-6 (two floating launchers with different icons, `AutoAwesomeOutlined` and `Chat`).

**Student, auth and fallback pages (comfortable density, S-01 to S-10)**

### S-01 · Course list — `/`

- **Source:** `src/pages/Courses.tsx:11` (route `src/App.tsx:60-66`); `src/components/HeroCarousel/HeroCarousel.tsx:15`, `src/components/ClassCard/ClassCard.tsx:21`, `src/components/ResponsiveGrid/ResponsiveGrid.tsx:17`; SR-1.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** S, I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute`: any signed-in user, consent redirect when configured. Instructors and admins are not redirected to `/admin` from here; they get the view-switch icon in SR-1 (seen live with an admin account `[L]`), and an instructor or admin who is enrolled in a class sees its card, as S does (the Experiment row needs a class in context, so it is absent here).
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Never recoloured:** the class cover images (`imageSnippetUrl`). · **Density overrides:** none.
- **Purpose:** Lets a signed-in user see their enrolled classes and open one.
- **Entry points:** the student sign-in redirect (`src/pages/Login.tsx:77`, `src/pages/GoogleRedirectHandler.tsx:48`) and its fallbacks (`GoogleRedirectHandler.tsx:59,66`); `UnprotectedRoute` for signed-in students visiting `/login`, `/register` or `/auth/callback` (`src/auth/UnprotectedRoute.tsx:23-25`); `AdminProtectedRoute` for users who are neither admin nor instructor (`src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:41`); the top-bar logo on student routes (`TopNav.tsx:124`) and the "Switch to Student View" icon (`:208-218`); the end of the consent flow (`src/pages/Consent.tsx:37,46`).
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. SR-1 with no class context (no switcher or label): logo, the view switch (I and A), logout — `Courses.tsx:39`.
  2. Hero banner (`HeroCarousel.tsx`): three full-bleed slides, a green (`#3f7d58` to `#1f4a34`), a blue (`#2f5d8a` to `#16324d`) and a violet (`#7a5c9e` to `#3d2c52`) gradient SVG with two translucent white circles each (`public/assets/images/bg-hero-1.svg`, `-2`, `-3`; alt texts "Decorative green gradient", "Decorative blue gradient", "Decorative violet gradient", `HeroCarousel.tsx:10-12`), cross-fading every 8 s over 1.2 s, infinite, with no dots or arrows; reduced motion shortens the fade to 250 ms and stops the zoom (`:17,21-32,70`). Over them a dark gradient and the `h1` "Welcome to {BRAND_LABEL}, {username}!" in white, bold, 2rem from `md`, where `{username}` is the part of the email before "@" (`:18-19,77-106`). Height 208 / 236 / 280 px by breakpoint, radius 4, up to 1440 px wide (`:35-48`).
  3. Class grid: `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(310px, 1fr))`, gap 40 px, 48 px below the hero (`ResponsiveGrid.tsx:17-31`; `Courses.tsx:60-71`). One `ClassCard` per enrolled class, a link `aria-label="Open {title}"` to `/{classId}` carrying `{ className }` in router state: a 252 px card with a 152 px cover (the class image under a faint bottom fade, or, with none or on load failure, a grey gradient with the italic `KiwiWordmark` in `grey.500` at 50% opacity), and a content panel overlapping the cover by 16 px (28 px on hover or focus) with a translucent paper fill and backdrop blur (reduced-transparency and reduced-motion variants exist); title (2-line clamp), instructor (one line) — `ClassCard.tsx:7-229`. The fallbacks differ: `Courses.tsx` passes "Class" and "TBD", while the card falls back to "Unnamed class" and "Instructor TBD" (`Courses.tsx:64-65`; `ClassCard.tsx:30-31`).
  4. A 120 px spacer; the surface is `grey.100` in a container up to 1440 px with a 32 px top margin — `:40-58,73`.

- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[T]`: the hero, headline and one class card (the demo class); the tour saw a violet-to-black slide on one load and a green-to-black one on another, a large decorative circle, and a light-grey canvas with large unused space beside one card.
  - `m:none` Loading `[S]`: **none**; the grid is empty until the request returns, with no skeleton or spinner (`Courses.tsx:14-30`).

  - `m:none` Success `[S]`: none; nothing is submitted from this page.

### S-02 · Materials — `/:classID`

- **Source:** `src/pages/ClassChat.tsx:11` (route `src/App.tsx:120`, inside SR-2), which renders only `PDFComponent` (`src/components/Chat/PDFComponent.tsx:65`) and so `PDFViewerForStudents` (`src/components/PDFViewer/PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:89`). Despite its name the page holds no chat: chat is the global panel SR-6 (`ClassChat.tsx:7-10`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** S, I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` (`src/App.tsx:112-124`); class access is decided by the backend. **Entry visibility:** the first tab, "Materials", of every class. **Role-specific chrome (I, A):** SR-1's view-switch icon and SR-6's Experiment toggle row (SR-6e); students have neither. The student comment and summary reads need an enrollment (`../kiwi/src/document/document.service.ts:1512`), so an unenrolled instructor or admin sees no comment pins and no summary banner.
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** the PDF pages (react-pdf pages on a white wrapper, `PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:660-683`). **Never recoloured:** the rendered PDF canvas and its figures; the "💬" glyph on comment pins. · **Density overrides:** the PDF pages and summary text are reading surfaces (comfortable); the icon rail, the "Class Materials" drawer, the 44 px viewer toolbar and the summary banner are tool chrome (compact).
- **Purpose:** Lets an enrolled student pick a lecture or recitation PDF from the class's list and read it page by page, while the open PDF and page are shared with the global chat.
- **Entry points:** a class card on S-01 (`src/pages/Courses.tsx:62-69`); tab "Materials" (`src/pages/ClassLayout.tsx:52,130-136`); the class switcher, which keeps the suffix; the chat's navigation actions to `/{classId}` and `/{classId}?pdfId=…&page=…` (`GlobalChatModal.tsx:68-91`) — no code reads `pdfId` or `page` from the URL (grep), so the query has no effect; the chat's citation buttons "[Page N]" switch the open PDF through context (`src/components/Chat/ChatMessages.tsx:394,408`).
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. SR-1 and the SR-2 tab bar. `ClassChat` pushes tab "materials" and mirrors class id, PDF id, 0-based page, material type and `pdfContent` to the global chat (`ClassChat.tsx:26-54`).
  2. Fallback `<h2>Loading class...</h2>`, in effect unreachable because SR-2 shows a spinner first (`ClassChat.tsx:56-62`; `pages/ClassLayout.tsx:363-376`).
  3. Icon rail, 48 px wide, holding one 36 px icon button with a folder glyph, native `title="Class materials"` and no aria-label; it toggles the drawer — `PDFComponent.tsx:376-408`.
  4. Viewer toolbar, 44 px: the current file name; icon-only buttons with aria-label only — "previous page", the label "{current} / {total}" (or "– / –"), "next page", "zoom out", "{n}%" (100%, step 0.2, min 0.5, max 3), "zoom in", "fullscreen" (which fullscreens only the scroll area) — `PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:540-616`. While no document is chosen the whole viewer, toolbar included, is replaced by the bare line "Loading your class lectures..." with no spinner (`:427-429`).
  5. Scroll area on a literal `#EDEBF1`, 20 px padding: a centred spinner while loading; the error panel; or the page stack. Each page sits on a white wrapper with a shadow `0 1px 4px rgba(28,12,48,0.14)`; **the current page carries a 2 px outline in `primary.main` (`#6a1b9a`)**, marking the page the AI has in context; text and annotation layers are on; professor comments appear as 24 px round blue pins (`#1976d2`) that open a 280 px popover `m:ov:comment-popover` — `PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:618-702,684-693,362-411`.
  6. Overlay `m:loaded`, the "Class Materials" drawer, open by default, 248 px, overlaying the left of the viewer (`PDFComponent.tsx:423-439`): title "Class Materials", an icon-only close, a segmented switch "Lecture" · "Recitation", then the file list (three skeleton rows while loading; "No documents"; one row per file showing the raw file name and a "✓" on the selected one). Picking a row loads that PDF and keeps the drawer open — `:457-565`.
  7. Overlay `m:ov:summary-banner`, the summary banner: a floating Paper, blue `#1976d2`, "Professor added {n} summary" / "Professor added {n} summaries", a filled white "Read" and an icon-only close; after dismissal a round blue book button with a red count badge re-shows it — `PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:465-538`.
  8. Overlay `m:ov:summaries-dialog`, Dialog "Document Summaries": a count, per summary "Summary {n}", the text and "Added by:" with the author name or email, "No summaries available for this document.", filled "Close" — `PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:715-778`.
  9. Overlay `m:native:pdf-password`: the browser's own `prompt()` "Enter the password to open this PDF file." for password-protected PDFs (react-pdf default, unverified at runtime).
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default (loaded) `[T]`: the toolbar shows "1 / 1" and "100%", the page has a purple outline, the drawer lists the class's files with the selected one tinted and ticked, and the Lecture / Recitation switch.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: three skeleton rows in the drawer plus "Loading your class lectures..."; after picking a row the same line until the URL arrives; then a spinner with "– / –"; per page the library's "Loading page…" (`PDFComponent.tsx:297-301,516-521`; `PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:576,633-643`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: the drawer shows "No documents" while the viewer keeps "Loading your class lectures..." **indefinitely**, with no dedicated empty copy and no spinner (`PDFComponent.tsx:201-202,522-527`) (SF-33).
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: red text "Couldn't load this PDF. This can happen on a slow or unstable network connection." with a filled "Retry" (`PDFViewerForStudent.tsx:431-451`). Document-list and document-URL failures have no catch, so the skeletons or the loading line persist; comment and summary failures are console-only (`PDFComponent.tsx:157-160,190-253,286-312`).
  - `m:none` Success `[S]`: none; the chosen PDF and page are saved silently to `localStorage` (`materialsPdf_{classId}`, `PDFComponent.tsx:39,314-334`).
  - Page-specific `[S]`: no search UI on this page; no disabled controls (previous, next and zoom clamp silently); the last PDF and page are restored per class; only documents of type "class materials" or "recitation" are listed (`PDFComponent.tsx:362-364`).
- **Primary CTA:** none designated; the main action is choosing a file row (a text row, not filled). Filled buttons: "Retry" (error only), "Read" (banner), "Close" (dialog).
- **Exit / next:** tab "Scratchpad" → S-03; app tabs → S-04; the class switcher; the global chat can navigate back here.

### S-03 · Code space — `/:classID/code`

- **Source:** `src/pages/ClassIDE.tsx:68` (route `src/App.tsx:121`, inside SR-2) → `src/components/CodeInterpreter/CodeInterpreter.tsx` → `IDE.tsx:72`; `FileTabs.tsx`, `Pyodide.tsx`, `WebR.tsx`; workers `public/assets/pyodide.worker.js`. `IDE.css` is not imported anywhere.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** S, I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only. **Entry visibility / feature gate:** the feature flag `RLanguageClass` (a user-level grant anywhere, a class-level grant for this class) shows the language select and, for R, the "Plots" and "Vars" tabs (`ClassIDE.tsx:132-139`; `IDE.tsx:429-460,605-610`). No role check. **Role-specific chrome (I, A):** SR-1's view-switch icon and SR-6's Experiment toggle row (SR-6e); students have neither.
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** none (the editor, output console and code blocks follow the mode and are not paper). **Never recoloured:** R plot images (PNG data URLs) and uploaded image previews (`IDE.tsx:331-332,374-384,657-665`). · **Density overrides:** the file-tab bar, upload row, language select, editor overlay buttons and output tab strip are tool chrome (compact); the output text is the nearest thing to a reading surface.
- **Purpose:** A scratch editor where a student writes and runs Python (R if the class has it), reads the output, and can hand the code and output to Kiwi Chat.
- **Entry points:** tab "Scratchpad" (`src/pages/ClassLayout.tsx:53,130-136`); a typed URL; the class switcher; the chat's code-block button "Import to Scratchpad" (`src/components/Chat/ChatMessages.tsx:110,217-219`), which stores the code, navigates here and closes the chat (`GlobalChatModal.tsx:101-109`; loaded at `ClassIDE.tsx:146-154`).
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. SR-1 and the SR-2 tab bar. The page tells the chat it is the tab "materials", view "code", app slug "codegen", tutoring mode "guidance", and sends the code (first 6,000 characters), output (first 2,000) and language as context (`ClassIDE.tsx:91-111,187-201`).
  2. Page frame: 16 px padding; an inner column of 960 px by default (minimum 480, maximum 100%), its width stored in `localStorage` `ideEditorWidth` and changed by a drag handle on its right edge (aria-label "resize editor") — `ClassIDE.tsx:252-269,298-329`.
  3. The "card": a full-height stack on `background.default`, with **no page title, heading, border, radius or shadow**. "Code Space" is only the first tab's label (`ClassIDE.tsx:143`); the document title is static "Kiwi" (`index.html:7`) — `IDE.tsx:387-392`.
  4. File-tab bar (aria-label "basic tabs example"): the first tab "Code Space" (no close), then a tab per opened file with an icon-only close button with no label — `FileTabs.tsx:162-187`.
  5. Upload row: an outlined small button "Upload" with a cloud icon wrapping a hidden multi-file input; then one **filled** 30 px button per file in the sandbox (uploaded names, or `code-<timestamp>.txt` from Save Code) that opens it as a tab — `FileTabs.tsx:196-255`.
  6. Language selector, only with `allowR`: a select with options "Python" and "R" and the caption "Python" or "R Language" — `IDE.tsx:429-460`.
  7. Editor (Ace): theme "clouds", 14 px, mode python / r / text, border `1px solid alpha(divider, 0.2)`, radius 4; starts empty unless restored from `localStorage` `ideState_{classId}`. Colours from the Ace theme: editor `#FFFFFF`, gutter `#ebebeb`, **active line `#FFFBD1` (pale yellow)**, selection `#BDD5FC` (`node_modules/ace-builds/src-noconflict/theme-clouds.js`). A `.txt` tab shows that file; other types show the editable text "This file type is not supported."; a lost buffer shows "File is no longer available. Please re-upload." — `IDE.tsx:463-486,313-337`.
  8. Editor overlay controls at the bottom right: an icon-only **Run** (play, `color="primary"`) and an icon-only **Upload** (file-upload icon, `color="info"`, which is `#1976d2` blue), neither with a label or tooltip — `IDE.tsx:487-521`. Run opens the Snackbar at once.
  9. Output tab strip: "Output"; for R also "Plots ({n})" and "Vars ({n})"; output panel: monospace `<pre>` showing `{output || "Output will appear here."}`; "No plots generated."; a "Vars" table with "Name" and "Preview" or "No variables." — `IDE.tsx:586-737`.
  10. Bottom action row, three **filled** buttons: "Move to Chat", "Check Answer", "Save Code" — `IDE.tsx:741-817`.
  11. Overlays: a Snackbar `m:success` "Code executed and files updated." (bottom centre, 3,000 ms, `IDE.tsx:576-583`); the browser's own `prompt()` `m:native:input-prompt` for every `input("…")` call in user code (`:147-158`); the Kiwi Chat panel `m:to:SR-6` opened with a prefilled prompt by "Move to Chat" and "Check Answer" (`ClassIDE.tsx:245-249`).
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[T]`: one tab "Code Space", an empty editor, "Output will appear here.", the three bottom buttons; Upload (outlined) and a language select where allowed.
  - `m:none` Loading `[S]`: **no loading UI for either runtime.** Pyodide's worker is created when the module first loads (inferred from the import chain, not observed) and loads Pyodide from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.25.0/full/pyodide.js` (`public/assets/pyodide.worker.js:3,12-32`); WebR loads from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/webr@0.6.0/dist/` on the first R run (`WebR.tsx:22-27`). The only feedback is the Snackbar at click.
  - `m:loaded` Empty `[S]`: "Output will appear here." (also after a run that printed nothing), "No plots generated.", "No variables.".
  - `m:r-tabs` R output tabs `[S]`: with the language select on R the output strip adds "Plots ({n})" and "Vars ({n})"; their panels read "No plots generated." and "No variables." when empty and otherwise show a plot image or the "Name" / "Preview" table (`IDE.tsx:586-737`).
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: Python exceptions replace stdout with the raw traceback text in the same `<pre>` with no error styling (`pyodide.worker.js:235-236`; `IDE.tsx:229-231`); R errors arrive in the captured console text or as `evalError.message`; a guard string "Package installation/loading is not supported in the browser R environment. Only base packages are available." (`WebR.tsx:52-65,205-209`). Runtime failures (CDN unreachable) show nothing: neither worker has an `onerror` handler (inferred).
  - `m:success` Success `[S]`: the Snackbar shows at click **before the run finishes**, so it appears whatever the outcome; Save Code adds a file button with no confirmation.
  - Page-specific `[S]`: no running indicator and Run stays clickable; no control is ever disabled; "Check Answer" does not check anything, it only fills the chat input; "Save Code" does not download; files and file tabs are lost when the student leaves the tab, only the code persists (debounced 400 ms) (`ClassIDE.tsx:140-182`).

### S-04 · Kiwi App (student host frame) — `/:classID/app/:appSlug`

- **Source:** `src/pages/ClassAppPage.tsx:22` (route `src/App.tsx:122`, inside SR-2) rendering `ClassAppView` (`src/pages/ClassAppView.tsx:35`). **Only the host frame is specified; the embedded app's content is out of scope.**
- **Roles (Appendix A):** S, I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` (`src/App.tsx:112-124`). **Entry visibility:** a tab in SR-2, labelled `tabLabel || name`, for each app enabled in the class; the tab list is not role-filtered (`src/pages/ClassLayout.tsx:106-114,262-278`). On a hard load of this URL the enabled-app list is empty, so the layout replaces the route with the first tab, "Materials" (R-5, seen live on 2026-10-16 with an admin account `[L]`: the typed URL `/local-css-demo/app/ics-r-lab` ended at `/local-css-demo` with no iframe; `ClassLayout.tsx:85,117-128,192-207`). **Role-specific chrome (I, A):** SR-1's view-switch icon and SR-6's Experiment toggle row (SR-6e); students have neither.
- **Density:** comfortable (the host chrome); the embedded app sets its own. · **Paper surfaces:** the Kiwi App iframe (`ClassAppView.tsx:656-669`): the embedded document stays light in dark mode (G5). **Never recoloured:** everything inside the iframe. · **Density overrides:** none drawn by the host.
- **Purpose:** Looks up one of the class's apps and embeds its class-tab UI in a full-height iframe as a tab of the student class view, passing class and user context and brokering the app's AI-chat, token, navigation and API-proxy requests.
- **Entry points:** the app tab in SR-2; a chat reply carrying a navigation action with target tab "app" (`src/components/Chat/ChatCore.tsx:894-900`; `GlobalChatModal.tsx:84-88`); `kiwi:navigate` from an embedded app (`ClassAppView.tsx:508-546`); the class switcher, which keeps the `/app/{slug}` suffix.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. SR-1 and the SR-2 tab bar; the content area shows SR-2's spinner until the class loads.
  2. Lookup: a centred spinner with "Loading app..." (`ClassAppPage.tsx:133-151`).
  3. Lookup error: a centred red Alert with the text or "App not found": "Missing class ID or app slug", `App "{appSlug}" is not enabled for this class`, "Failed to load app"; no retry (`:153-168,86,102,124`).
  4. Iframe-load error: a centred red Alert "Failed to load {appName}", no retry (`ClassAppView.tsx:391-395,601-615`).
  5. Default frame: a full-size flex box, minimum height `calc(100vh - 180px)`, holding a loading veil (`background.paper`, spinner and "Loading {appName}...") over the iframe. The iframe is mounted at once, has `title={appName}`, `border: none`, `display: none` until `load`, no host-set background, and the sandbox "allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox" (no `allow-downloads`); its `src` is the class-tab UI URL, else the app's `baseUrl`, plus `classId`, `appId`, `userId` and `uiSlug` — `ClassAppView.tsx:618-669,373-384`. **No toolbar, header or retry surrounds it.**
  6. Bridge handshake (no visible status): `kiwi:ready` → `kiwi:context` (class, user, role defaulting to "student", capabilities); `kiwi:askAI` streams a Kiwi Agent answer back; `kiwi:updateContext` feeds the floating chat; `kiwi:apiRequest` proxies named operations, with error texts such as "unknown op: {op}", "no class context yet", "missing scope(s): {list}"; `kiwi:navigate`, `kiwi:requestToken` and `kiwi:setChatDisplayMode` — `ClassAppView.tsx:424-578`.
  7. Over the frame, from the host: the Kiwi Chat launcher (SR-6), whose default resting place is **bottom-left on app tabs** (24 px from the left, 96 px above the bottom) because this page sets the active tab to "app"; the code comment says apps place their own primary actions bottom-right (`src/pages/ClassAppPage.tsx:42`; `GlobalChatButton.tsx:90-95,131-138`). Opening the chat panel in modal or side-panel mode dims the page, the iframe included.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[T]`: the app fills the content area (the tour saw "CSS R Lab" with its own wordmark, eyebrow, cards and left nav, English and Chinese headings mixed).
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: "Loading app..." then the veil "Loading {appName}..."; the veil is the only progress indicator.
  - `m:none` Empty: none; a missing app gives the lookup error; with neither a class-tab UI nor a `baseUrl` the iframe gets an empty `src` and the host shows no message (outcome unverified).
  - `m:error:lookup` `m:error:iframe` Error `[S]`: blocks 3 and 4, fixed English strings; the real errors are logged only.
  - `m:none` Success: none.
  - Page-specific `[S]`: changing the class or slug re-runs the lookup; leaving the page clears the chat's app context; the lookup treats an app as enabled when it appears in the class list, without checking `isEnabled` (`ClassAppPage.tsx:99-104`); the iframe `src` may change, and reload, if the user id resolves after the first render (derived).
- **Primary CTA:** none drawn by the host. The only host-owned filled control in the region is the "Open Kiwi Chat" launcher.
- **Exit / next:** other tabs; app-initiated back, forward, home and class-scoped paths; the class switcher; chat navigation actions.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the veil and error Alerts; the paper boundary; the launcher's size and elevation (position is Stage 2, TD-18).
<!-- copy:S-04:start -->
- **Copy (Phase 5):** 7 strings revised (rules C5, C9); every row is in the [Revision index](#revision-index). Only the host frame's words are in scope; the embedded app's own text is not (G5). The bridge replies sent to the app ("unknown op", "no class context yet") are developer-facing messages to the app's code, not interface text.
  - `S-04.01` `Loading app...` → `Loading app…` · C5 · the ellipsis character (C5: Yifrah; G12 voice rule)
  - `S-04.02` `Missing class ID or app slug` → `Couldn't open this app. The link is missing the class or the app. Open the app from its tab in your class.` · C9 · "Slug" is developer vocabulary. (C9: Yifrah; Nielsen #9)
  - `S-04.03` `App "{appSlug}" is not enabled for this class` → `Couldn't open {appSlug}. It isn't turned on for this class. Ask your instructor to turn it on.` · C9 · what happened, why, and what to do (C9: Yifrah; Nielsen #9)
  - `S-04.04` `App not found` → `Couldn't open this app. The app wasn't found. Go back to your class and try its tab again.` · C9 · what happened, why, and what to do (C9: Yifrah; Nielsen #9)
  - `S-04.05` `Failed to load app` → `Couldn't open this app. The server didn't respond as expected. Try again.` · C9 · what happened, why, and what to do (C9: Yifrah; Nielsen #9)
  - `S-04.06` `Failed to load {appName}` → `Couldn't load {appName}. The server didn't respond as expected. Try again.` · C9 · what happened, why, and what to do (C9: Yifrah; Nielsen #9)
  - `S-04.07` `Loading {appName}...` → `Loading {appName}…` · C5 · the ellipsis character (C5: Yifrah; G12 voice rule)
<!-- copy:S-04:end -->
- **Tour defects (in boundary):** TD-C1 (host surfaces; heuristic 4, sev 1); TD-07 (heuristic 4, sev 1, via SR-1); TD-05, TD-09, TD-10, TD-11 (heuristic 4, sev 1), TD-12 (heuristic 2, sev 1) and TD-13 (heuristic 1, sev 2), all via SR-6.
- **Out of boundary, recorded:** TD-17 (the embedded app styles itself: lowercase "kiwi" wordmark with a purple full stop, purple eyebrow, cards, left workspace nav; it changes only where it reads the public tokens, G5); TD-18 (on this page the launcher sits bottom-left and covers the app's sidebar progress label "Questions completed 2/5"); the tour's mixed-script headings ("… NA 与均值", "Demo · CSS 数据分析作业") are the G7 mixed-script case, rendered in the embedded app's own text.
- **Source-found:** SF-51 (host differences, see A-12).

### S-05 · Sign-in — `/login`

- **Source:** `src/pages/Login.tsx:25` (route `src/App.tsx:68-74`); SR-5 (split variant); `src/components/Brand/KiwiWordmark.tsx`, `src/components/GoogleLoginButton/GoogleLoginButton.tsx:21`.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** all. **Guard (code):** `UnprotectedRoute`: signed-out only. A signed-in user is redirected to `/consent` first if consent is required and missing, otherwise to `/admin` (instructor, admin) or `/` (D-2; `src/auth/UnprotectedRoute.tsx:15-26`).
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** none.
- **Purpose:** Signs a returning user in with email and password, or with Google where enabled.
- **Entry points:** any `ProtectedRoute` or `AdminProtectedRoute` visited signed out (`src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:51-53`; `AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:15-17`); sign-out (R-3); the middleware's session end, `/login?timeout=true` (`src/utils/middleware.ts:46-52,64-71,80-88`); the "Log in" link on S-06 (`src/pages/Register.tsx:79-86`); a typed URL.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. SR-5's aside from `md` (the wordmark, the quote, the sub-line).
  2. Session-expired banner, a warning Alert "Your session has expired. Please log in again.", only with `?timeout=true` — `Login.tsx:100-117`.
  3. Below `md`, `InstitutionLogo` above the heading — `:119-128`.
  4. `h1` "Welcome back to " followed by the `KiwiWordmark` (Montserrat 800 italic), `nowrap` from `md` — `:129-147`; the subtitle "Continue learning with AI-powered support." — `:148-159`.
  5. An error Alert "Login failed. Please check your credentials and try again." — `:161-168,92-94`.
  6. With password login on (the default): a form with "Email" (type email, required) and "Password" (required, with an icon button aria-labelled "Show password" / "Hide password"), and a full-width filled pill button "Login" (radius 999, 48 px) — `:170-264`.
  7. With Google on: a divider "OR" (only beside the password form) and an outlined `GoogleLoginButton` "Continue with Google" with the four-colour Google mark (literal brand hex values) — `:266-280`; `GoogleLoginButton.tsx:60-66`.
  8. With neither on: a warning Alert reading **"No sign-in method is enabled. Unset VITE_DISABLE_PASSWORD_LOGIN or set VITE_ENABLE_GOOGLE_LOGIN=true."** — `:282-287`.
  9. The footer line: with Google on "Don't have an account? " and a link "Create one" to `/register`; otherwise "Need an account? Ask your administrator." — `:289-313`.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[T]`: the aside, "Welcome back to Kiwi", a purple pill "Login", "Need an account? Ask your administrator."
  - `m:timeout-banner` Session expired `[T]`: an orange-tinted box above the heading.
  - `m:submitting` Submitting `[S]`: the fields and the visibility toggle are disabled and the button shows a spinner and "Signing in…" (`:241-264`).
  - `m:none` Loading, empty: none (the page is a form; the only wait is the submitting state above).
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: the error Alert; typing clears it. Every failure gets the same message, whether wrong credentials, network, or a failing profile or consent call (`:90-94,185-188`).
  - `m:to:S-01` `m:to:A-01` Success `[S]`: the role is fetched; instructors and admins go to `/admin`, everyone else to `/`; if the role call fails the user is treated as a student (`:59-89`).
  - `m:config:google` `m:config:google-only` `m:config:neither` Configuration `[S]`: password only; password plus Google (the divider, the Google button, "Create one"); Google only (no form, no divider); neither (the warning above).
- **Primary CTA:** "Login" → authenticates and redirects (`:241-264`). The Google button is outlined in this layout.
- **Exit / next:** S-01 (students) or `/admin` (R-1 then A-01); S-06 through "Create one"; Google through `{VITE_BACKEND_URL}/auth?frontend={origin}` (`GoogleLoginButton.tsx:29`), returning to S-07.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the tagline and the aside (SR-5), the wordmark (the one place Montserrat stays), a mascot at sign-in (G9), stored Display preferences honoured (there is no top bar here).
- **Companion (Phase 4):** the `h1` display line sits beside the idle still (the lock's wording): `companion.slot.signin` 96 px from `md` and `companion.slot.inline` 64 px below it at the form column's text edge (24 px right of the ruler, 12 at 390), the line to its right with a 24 px gap, top-aligned, wrapping as needed; in light mode the still is placed by its ink box (the slot shifts left by the drawing's ink inset, 15.3 % of the slot, so the ink meets the text edge), in dark mode the `--companion-backing` disc is the box; the aside gets no mascot (SR-5). Still only: nothing animates on sign-in. The stored Kiwi animation choice is read here for the chat panel's sake, not for this slot.

Kept as is, because it already follows the guide: Email; Password; Show password; Hide password; Signing in…; Continue with Google. The aside's tagline and sub-line are SR-5. ### S-08 · MCP OAuth authorize — `/authorize`

- **Source:** `src/pages/MCPAuthorize.tsx:14` (route `src/App.tsx:84-87`); `AuthLayout` (centred variant), `FormCard` (glass), `LogoBox` (`src/components/LogoBox/LogoBox.tsx`), `GoogleLoginButton`.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** "per route guard". **Guard (code):** **none** (D-3): the route has no wrapper, so signed-out and signed-in visitors both reach it, and the consent redirect never applies. **Entry visibility:** valid only with `?oauth_pending=true`.
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** none. **Never recoloured:** the logo image (`LOGO_URL`, "shown as-is") and the campus photo behind the page (`AuthLayout.tsx:126`; the file is missing, SF-01). · **Density overrides:** none.
- **Purpose:** Kiwi, acting as the OAuth authorization server for an external MCP client, lets the visitor sign in (if needed) and approve the pending request, then sends the browser to the client's redirect URL.
- **Entry points:** an external MCP client opens the backend `GET /auth/authorize`, which validates the request and redirects to `{FRONTEND_URL}/authorize?oauth_pending=true` (`../kiwi/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:260-324`). Nothing inside the app links here (grep).
- **Content blocks (in order):** the decision order is invalid flag (`MCPAuthorize.tsx:100`), then signed in (`:120`), then signed out (`:175`).
  1. Shell: `AuthLayout` centred (a full-viewport campus photo under a gradient from `primary.dark` at about 72% alpha) around a glass `FormCard` (elevation 12, `rgba(255,255,255,0.2)` fill, blur, white text); no top bar or sidebar. The chat launcher appears only in the signed-in view — `AuthLayout.tsx:118-136`; `FormCard.tsx:9-37`.
  2. View A, flag missing or not exactly "true", for everyone: the logo; `h6` in the error colour "Invalid Authorization Request"; "This page is only accessible during an OAuth authorization flow."; no button or link — `:100-117`.
  3. View B, signed in: the logo; `h6` "Authorize Application"; "An application is requesting access to your account."; "Signed in as: {user.username}" (the account email); an error banner that can never carry a message; a contained full-width "Authorize" (a spinner replaces the label); an outlined full-width "Cancel" — `:119-173`.
  4. View C, signed out: an info banner "Sign in to authorize the application to access your account."; an error banner; the logo (alt "{INSTITUTION_NAME} logo", 140 px); with password login on, a form with "Your Email", "Password" and a contained full-width "Login & Authorize"; with Google on, a contained pill "Login with Google"; with both off, only the banner and logo and no message — `:175-261`.
  5. Overlays: none.
- **States:**
  - `m:view:invalid` `m:view:signed-in@S,I,A` `m:view:signed-out@out` Default `[S]`: View B or C per sign-in state; View A without the flag.
  - `m:submitting` Loading `[S]`: no page-level loading; only an in-button 24 px spinner replaces the label; controls are disabled while authorising with no reason text (`:155,165,223,234,243`).
  - `m:none` Empty: none.
  - `m:view:invalid` Error `[S]`: invalid flag → View A. For a signed-in "Authorize" failure every error is caught once, logged to the console, and the user is sent to `/` (`:55-61`); the message "Authorization failed" is never shown. For signed-out login the server's reply arrives as the browser's own response to a native form POST, for example the API text "Invalid email or password" (backend `../kiwi/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:157,164`; inferred).
  - `m:to:S-01` Success `[S]`: **no success screen.** Signed-in "Authorize" posts with a bearer token; the code comment says the cross-origin redirect is blocked and treated as success, then `navigate('/')` (`:35-62`; unverified at runtime). Signed-out "Login & Authorize" submits a hidden form to `{basePath}/auth/oauth-login`, the browser leaves the SPA and the backend redirects to the client; neither path stores `authToken` or calls `login()` (`:65-98`).
  - Page-specific `[S]`: only `oauth_pending` is read; the page **never names the requesting application or its scopes** (`:26-27,129-131`); "Cancel" navigates to `/` and calls no API, so the pending request is not declined; empty fields can be submitted (no `required`, no `type="email"`); if both login methods are on, two filled buttons show together.
- **Primary CTA:** View B "Authorize" → POST `{basePath}/auth/oauth-authorize` (`:150-159`); View C "Login & Authorize" → native form POST (`:237-246`) and "Login with Google" when enabled; View A none.
- **Exit / next:** View A none (browser back); View B success or any caught error → the client's `redirectUrl` or `/` (S-01), "Cancel" → `/`; View C leaves to the backend or Google and then the client's callback.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the mascot slot at sign-in and the error state; the glass `FormCard` (blur, translucent fill) conflicts with the brief's "no glass effects" (SF-63); the missing campus photo.
- **Companion (Phase 4):** the centred card's heading is preceded by `companion.slot.inline` 64 px (all widths): the idle still in views B and C, the error still in view A ("Invalid Authorization Request"); on the `--companion-backing` disc in dark mode. Still only.
<!-- copy:S-08:start -->
- **Copy (Phase 5):** 10 strings revised (rules C6, C8, C9, C11, C16); every row is in the [Revision index](#revision-index). Kept as is, because it already follows the guide: Password; Cancel; Signed in as: {username}. The page never names the requesting app (SF-41, a flow change outside Stage 1), so the consent wording says what is being granted and when to continue, and does not claim to know the app.
  - `S-08.01` `Invalid Authorization Request` → `This request isn't valid` · C6 · Names the problem in the reader's terms. (C6: Podmajersky terminology agreement; Nielsen #4)

### S-09 · Consent — `/consent`

- **Source:** `src/pages/Consent.tsx:16` (route `src/App.tsx:104-110`); `src/components/PDFViewer/PDFViewer.tsx`.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** "per route guard". **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute`: any signed-in user. **The page only exists when `VITE_CONSENT_FORM_URL` is set:** without it the component returns `<Navigate to="/" replace />` (`Consent.tsx:45-47`; R-4). The consent gate that sends users here is `ProtectedRoute`, `UnprotectedRoute` and `AdminProtectedRoute` while `user.consent` is false (`src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:55-58`).
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** the consent PDF, rendered continuously by `PDFViewer pdfFile={formUrl} continuous` (`Consent.tsx:56`). **Never recoloured:** the PDF pages. · **Density overrides:** the PDF toolbar (tool chrome, compact).
- **Purpose:** Shows the consent document and records the user's agreement before they can use Kiwi.
- **Entry points:** the consent redirect from any wrapper (`ProtectedRoute.tsx:55-58`; `UnprotectedRoute.tsx:15-18`; `AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:19-22`); a typed URL.
- **Content blocks (in order):** the page uses raw HTML elements and no layout, top bar or card:
  1. `<h1>Consent Form</h1>` — `Consent.tsx:52`.
  2. `<p>Please read the document below and accept to continue.</p>` — `:53`.
  3. The PDF viewer (toolbar "Search", "Thumbnails", "First", "Previous", "Page", "Next", "Last", "Zoom out", "Zoom in", "Fit width", "Open / print", "Fullscreen"; `PDFViewer.tsx:106-203`).
  4. Only when `user.consent === false`: a form with a date field "Today's date" (default today), a checkbox "I agree to participate" and a contained "Submit", disabled until the date is non-empty and the box is ticked, with no reason shown — `:58-98`.
  5. SR-6 launcher (the user is signed in).
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: as above.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: the viewer's own "Loading PDF…".
  - `m:none` Empty: none.
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: the viewer's red Alert "Couldn't load this PDF." with "Retry" (`PDFViewer.tsx:76-89`); a failed submit is `console.error` only and the user sees nothing (`Consent.tsx:39-41`).
  - `m:to:S-01` Success `[S]`: the call succeeds, the user is updated with `consent: true` (the system role is dropped and re-fetched) and sent to `/` (`:34-38`); no confirmation text.
  - `m:consented` Page-specific `[S]`: with `consent` already true the form is not rendered and the page only shows the document.
- **Primary CTA:** "Submit" (contained) → records consent and goes to S-01 (`:87-96`).
- **Exit / next:** S-01 on success; nothing else (no way out for a user who declines).
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the unstyled heading and paragraph take the type scale; the paper PDF; the form controls.

### S-10 · Not found — `*`

- **Source:** `src/App.tsx:194-198`: `{ path: "*", element: <div>Not found</div> }`, inside `RootLayout`.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** all. **Guard (code):** none, so signed-out visitors see it too.
- **Density:** comfortable · **Paper surfaces:** none.
- **Purpose:** Catches any URL no other route matches.
- **Entry points:** any path with two or more segments that no route matches, for example `/admin/typo` or `/a/b/c`; **the student OAuth return**, because `ProtectedRoute` navigates to `/class/{classId}` and `/class/{classId}/pdf/{pdfId}`, which are not routes (D-6, SF-03; `src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:31-35`). A **one-segment** unknown path such as `/typo` does *not* land here: it matches `/:classID`, so S-02 renders under SR-2 and the layout shows a spinner that never clears (SF-04).
- **Content blocks (in order):** one `<div>` holding the text "Not found". No heading, no layout, no top bar, no link back, no document title of its own. When signed in, SR-6's launcher is also on the page.
- **States:** `m:loaded` a single state, `[S]`. No loading, empty, error or success.
- **Primary CTA:** none.
- **Exit / next:** none on the page; the browser's back button, or the launcher.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the brief allows restyling the **content** of this existing catch-all route and a mascot illustration here (G9); no region, route or navigation may be added.
- **Companion (Phase 4):** the walk still (the standing bird) in `companion.slot.not-found` 96 px from `md` and `inline` 64 below it, on the ruled column above the `--text-2xl` line and the way back (Phase 5 copy), on the `--companion-backing` disc in dark mode. Still only.
<!-- copy:S-10:start -->
- **Copy (Phase 5):** 4 strings revised (rules C2, C6, C12); every row is in the [Revision index](#revision-index). The mascot (the standing bird) sits above the heading; the rest is these four strings. Inserted under the plan's never-dead-end constraint (an error or a not-found page always gives a way on, Yifrah): the two way-back controls, "Go to your classes" and "Sign in", are links to routes that already exist (`/` for a signed-in visitor, `/login` for a signed-out one), so they add no route and no region. They are the one piece of navigation this page gains, and the Stage 1 hooks line above ("no region, route or navigation may be added") is read as no new destination.
  - `S-10.01` `Not found` → `Page not found` · C6 · A heading that names the situation. (C6: Podmajersky terminology agreement; Nielsen #4) [SF-10]
  - `S-10.02` (none) → `The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved.` · C12 · Not-found pattern: what happened, the likely why, without blame. (C12: Redish; NN/g empty-state types; peak-end) [SF-10]

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/Analytics.tsx:229` (route `src/App.tsx:139`); `src/components/Analytics/AnalyticsDateRangeControl.tsx`, `StandaloneUserActivity.tsx`, `StandaloneDailySessions.tsx`, `StandaloneTopActions.tsx`, `StandaloneUserDuration.tsx`, `StandaloneUserEngine.tsx`, `StandaloneTopTokenUsers.tsx`, `chartXAxis.ts`, `chartAnimation.ts`; `src/components/DateTimeRangePicker/DateTimeRangePicker.tsx`; chart colours `src/Theme.ts:65-71`; frame SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader`: `Analytics.tsx:363-382`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5), plus an in-page check (D-7): after the first render `authControllerGetUserRole` runs and any role other than admin is sent to `/admin/classes`, while the data request starts regardless (`Analytics.tsx:241-252,320-324`); a failed role request goes to `/login`. - **Stage 1 hooks:** the KPI tile (Phase 3, applied in Phase 6, with a baseline or "none"); the chart palette and encoding rules (Phase 6); the empty and error states.
- **Data surfaces (Phase 6):** the chart and table specs of this page (`kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Chart tokens`; TD-36, SF-44). **Tiles (DW-6.3):** the four tiles are the Phase 3 KPI tile: label (`--type-label`), value (`--type-kpi-value`, tabular: `1,234`, `{n} min`), icon `--icon-default`, and a third line, which here reads "No earlier period to compare" (rows P6-A-03): the analytics API returns the chosen range only, and a prior period would be a second request (Stage 2). **Charts (DW-6.2, DW-6.4, DW-6.6):** (1) hourly and daily active users and (2) hourly and daily sessions, block 3: one series each, in `--chart-1` (the accent hue at the chart lightness); daily buckets are bars that grow from a `--chart-baseline` zero line (at most 24 px thick, a 4 px radius at the data end only, a 2 px gap between neighbours), hourly buckets a 2 px straight-segment line with no area fill (a daily range whose buckets would fall below 4 px each also draws as a line); no `monotone`, no gradient (TD-36); no entrance animation (`chartAnimation.ts` goes: the locked motion budget); the Y axis counts people or sessions with integer ticks (`allowDecimals={false}`; steps of 1, 2, 5 or 10) and names the unit; the line under the title states the unit, the bucket and the period, with its dates ("Users per day, the last 7 days (1 Oct – 7 Oct 2026)" for a preset, its sentence form with its dates in brackets; "Users per day, 1 Oct – 7 Oct 2026" for a custom range; "Sessions per hour, 17 Oct 2026" for one day; rows P6-A-03); X ticks read `1 Oct` and `14:00`, an hourly axis on one rhythm from midnight with no tick of its own for the last bucket (00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 for a day, never 23:00), and the tooltip `1 Oct 2026, 14:05` (the four `chartXAxis.ts` rows); the highest bucket carries its value as a direct label, haloed in `--chart-plot`, daily and hourly alike; gridlines are solid `--chart-grid` hairlines, horizontal only; ticks and labels are `--chart-tick-text`, never a series colour; a text summary, the period after "for", is the figure's caption: the `<figure>` is named by its title (`aria-labelledby`) and described by its caption (`aria-describedby`), and the chart's SVG is `aria-hidden` (Recharts `accessibilityLayer={false}`), so each is announced once. (3) Top actions, block 4: six nominal categories and one measure, so one series in `--chart-1` (the category is on the axis; today's colour per bar is retired), horizontal bars from zero sorted by count with "Other code actions" and "Other actions" last, the count at each bar's tip and no value axis (the labels are the values; the zero baseline stays), the label gutter as wide as the longest label ("Code and output sent to chat"), the line "Interactions by action, {range}", a summary. (4) User duration and (5) Model choice, block 4: part-to-whole with two or three parts of very different size, so the donuts stay, and the slices are categories, so they take categorical colour: Chat `--chart-1`, Scratchpad `--chart-2`; ChatGPT `--chart-1`, Qwen `--chart-2`, Unknown `--chart-other`; a 2 px `--chart-plot` gap between slices (the stroke in the surface colour, never a border), every slice carries a direct label, its name over its share (`ChatGPT` over `66%`, row P6-A-03), outside the ring, a thin slice (Unknown) joined to its label by a 1 px `--chart-tick-text` leader, so no slice is told by colour alone; the legend carries each value with its unit (`{hours: count hour}`; `{n: count request}`) and the centre the total with its unit; User duration's one unit is the hour, to two significant figures in the centre, the legend, the tooltip and the summary ("about 33 hours"; the legend's minutes, A-03.22, go; rows P6-A-03); the line under the title states the period; a summary each. **Colour (DW-6.4):** the only categorical colour on the page is on the two donuts; every other mark is `--chart-1`; no series colour is used as text; `--accent-solid` stays on controls; no red, purple or pink appears (SF-44 closed). **Empty:** a chart whose series is empty shows the empty-state line of Phase 5 (A-03.21, A-03.26, A-03.28) in the plot's place, never a zero-filled curve or six zero bars. **Tables (DW-6.5):** (6) Top token users, block 5, becomes the Phase 3 table (today a `List`): Rank (right-aligned, tabular, `--size-col-min-num`), User (the email or "(no email)", one line with an ellipsis and the full text on hover and focus, the id under it truncating the same way; `--size-col-min-text`), Sessions and Tokens (right-aligned tabular numerals, `1,234`, the unit in the header; `--size-col-min-num`), the chevron; the row opens the dialog. (7) Token usage detail, the overlay: Session ID (monospace; the columns take their content's widths, so the id is whole in the dialog at full width and is cut, one line at `--size-col-min-text` or more with the full id on hover and focus, only when the dialog is narrower), Start and End (`17 Oct 2026, 14:05`, A-03.31, `--size-col-min-date`; an open session's End is the em dash named "No value", A-03.54), Interactions (the header is row P6-A-03; its cells are bare numerals, right-aligned and tabular: a Phase 6 row supersedes A-03.52's New so the unit has one place per column) and Tokens (right-aligned tabular numerals, `1,234`); the sortable headers are buttons; every truncated span's full text is Phase 3's tooltip as `kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Chart tokens › Tables` gives it (the toggletip geometry, the cell's face, hoverable, dismissed by Escape, the span's ring inset −2 px).
