### A-04 · System email — `/admin/email`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/AdminEmail.tsx:61` (route `src/App.tsx:140-143`, wrapped in `AdminProtectedRoute`); `src/components/Email/RecipientSelector.tsx`, `EmailComposer.tsx`, `TemplatedEmailForm.tsx`; frame SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader`: `AdminEmail.tsx:267-271`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `AdminProtectedRoute` admits `isAdmin === true` **or** `systemRole === 'instructor'`; everyone else is redirected to `/` (`src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:39-42`), so instructors pass (D-1). **Entry visibility:** sidebar "System Email" is admin-only (`src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:68-73`, filter `:280-282`); the chat-agent sitemap marks it admin-only (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:72-76`).
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** the templated-email preview, an HTML `iframe` using `srcDoc` with no `sandbox` attribute, titled "Email Preview", 400 px high, inside a white box; and the plain-text pane (`src/components/Email/TemplatedEmailForm.tsx:434-487`). **Never recoloured:** the email HTML, whose colours come from the template's own CSS (Appendix C). · **Density overrides:** the preview and the 12-row and 8-row message inputs are reading surfaces (comfortable); tab bar, recipient list, template select and accordions are tool chrome.
- **Purpose:** An admin picks recipients (everyone, a role group, pending users, or one class), then sends a free-text email or one of three fixed templates, or browses the recipient lists.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "System Email"; the chat agent's navigation destination `email`; a typed URL. No other link found (repo-wide search).
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "Email Management"; description "Send emails to users and classes, or use an email template." — `AdminEmail.tsx:267-271`.
  2. Tab bar, icons before labels: "Custom Email", "Templated Email", "Email Lists"; only the active tab is mounted — `:273-280,53-59`.
  3. Tab "Custom Email" (`:282-296`): the shared recipient selector — select "Filter Recipients" (default "All Users ({n})"; options "All Students", "All Professors", "All Pending Users", "Pending Students", "Pending Professors", and per class "{className} ({n} active)" with an indented "Pending in {className} ({n})"), a search field with placeholder "Search by email...", an info Alert "{k} of {m} recipients selected" (plus " ({t} total selected)" when selections lie outside the filter), text buttons "Select All" and "Clear All", a scrollable list of rows (checkbox, email, outlined warning chip "pending", role text), and a success Alert "Total recipients selected: {n}" — `src/components/Email/RecipientSelector.tsx:129-340`; then the composer: fields "Subject" and "Message" (12 rows, placeholder "Compose your message..."), filled button "Send Email" — `src/components/Email/EmailComposer.tsx:85-177`.
  4. Tab "Templated Email" `m:loaded:templated` (`AdminEmail.tsx:298-345`): a second recipient selector with its own state; select "Email Template" ("Class Announcement" default, "Admin Notification", "Welcome Email"); the template form with a per-template info Alert and fields (Class Announcement: "Class Name", "Professor Name", "Announcement Message"; Admin Notification: "Notification Title", "Notification Message"; Welcome: "Frontend URL (Optional)"); a tinted preview panel with `h6` "Email Preview", "Subject:", tabs "HTML Preview" · "Plain Text" — `TemplatedEmailForm.tsx:393-491`; filled button "Send Templated Email" with a send icon — `AdminEmail.tsx:334-343`.
  5. Tab "Email Lists" `m:loaded:lists` (`:347-487`): `h6` "Email Lists Overview" and collapsed accordions "All Users ({n})", "Pending Users ({n})" and one "{className} ({n} students)" per class, each showing the first 50 rows (email, a chip with the raw status text "active" / "pending", role) and "... and {n} more users" / "Showing first 50 users only".
  6. Overlay `m:success` `m:error`: snackbar with a closable Alert, 6,000 ms — `:490-502`. The two select menus. No dialog, no drawer, **no confirm-before-send**.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded:custom` Default `[T]` (Templated tab and recipient picker seen): tab 0 active, filter "All Users ({n})", nothing selected ("0 of {n} recipients selected", the blue info bar the tour saw), "Send Email" disabled until Subject and Message hold text (`EmailComposer.tsx:170`).
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: a centred spinner from the route guard while `isAdmin` is undefined (`AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:24-37`); then a skeleton without the page header until users, classes, pending users and rosters resolve (`AdminEmail.tsx:257-264`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: selector "No users in this filter" or "No users found matching your search" (`RecipientSelector.tsx:281`); "No pending users" with "All users have been activated" (`AdminEmail.tsx:446-447`); a class with an empty roster renders an empty list with no text.
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: snackbar "Failed to load email data" (`:165-171`); a send failure shows an error Alert inside the composer with the API message or "Failed to send email" (`EmailComposer.tsx:80,87`) or an error snackbar "Failed to send templated email" (`AdminEmail.tsx:244-248`); zero recipients shows "No recipients selected" (`:180-187,215-222`).
  - `m:success` Success `[S]`: snackbars "Email sent successfully to {n} recipients" and "Templated email sent successfully to {n} recipients" (`:200-204,234-238`); the recipient selection clears.
  - `m:submitting` Page-specific `[S]`: "Send Email" is not disabled when zero recipients are selected; the check runs on click (`:180-187`). Disabled controls give no reason. **After a resolved Custom Email send the composer's `sending` flag is never reset**, so the button keeps reading "Sending..." and the fields stay disabled until the tab is switched (derived; `EmailComposer.tsx:69-82`). "Send Templated Email" is enabled as soon as the tab mounts and nothing validates the required fields (`TemplatedEmailForm.tsx:264-279`; `AdminEmail.tsx:339`). Preview fallback copy: "Preview will appear as you fill in the form fields..." (`TemplatedEmailForm.tsx:451,483`).
- **Primary CTA:** tab 1 "Send Email" → `emailControllerSendToUsers`; tab 2 "Send Templated Email" → `emailControllerSendTemplatedEmail` (`EmailComposer.tsx:167-174`; `AdminEmail.tsx:178-198,213-232`). No other filled button in the view.
- **Exit / next:** none; the page stays after sending (no router import).
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the paper preview and the template colours and copy (Phase 3 maps them to tokens; Phase 5 revises the copy; see Appendix C); empty-state frame for the recipient and list blocks.

### A-06 · System flags — `/admin/feature-flags`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/SystemWideFeatureFlags.tsx:9` (route `src/App.tsx:148`); `src/components/FeatureFlags/AddClassFeature.tsx`, `AddUserFeature.tsx`, `ListAllFeatures.tsx`; frame SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader`: `SystemWideFeatureFlags.tsx:31-35`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** sidebar "System Flags" is admin-only (`AdminLayout.tsx:80-85`); the sitemap key `feature-flags` (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:77-82`). No in-page role check.
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none (the DataGrid and form controls are tool chrome).
- **Purpose:** Lets an admin grant a named feature to every member of a class or to one user (optionally with an expiry), review all grants in a table and change a grant's expiry.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "System Flags"; the chat agent; a typed URL.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "Feature Flags"; description "Control staged feature access for classes and individual users." — `:31-35`.
  2. Section intro: `h2` "Add an assignment"; "Choose the narrowest scope possible and add an expiration for temporary access." — `:38-45`.
  3. Two add cards side by side from `lg`: "Class access" ("Enable a feature for every member of a class."; select "Class" whose options are **raw class IDs**; select "Feature" whose options are raw enum identifiers; datetime-local "Expiration (optional)" with the helper "Leave empty to keep the flag active indefinitely."; contained "Add class flag" / "Adding…") and "User access" ("Enable a feature for one specific user."; text field "User ID"; "Feature"; "Expiration (optional)"; contained "Add user flag") — `AddClassFeature.tsx:86-164`; `AddUserFeature.tsx:69-130`.
  4. Card "Active assignments": "Review scopes, targets, and expiration dates for all feature flags."; outlined "Refresh"; an error Alert; a MUI X `DataGrid` (auto height, 10 rows per page, row-click selection off) with columns "Feature", "Scope" (chip "Class" / "User"), "Target" (raw id), "Expiration" (local date-time or a red chip "Expired" or an outlined green chip "No expiration"), and an unlabelled last column with a text button "Edit" — `ListAllFeatures.tsx:179-232`.
  5. Overlays: a snackbar `m:success` `m:error` in each add card (bottom centre, 4,000 ms; "Class feature flag added." / "User feature flag added."; `AddClassFeature.tsx:67-72,169-178`, `AddUserFeature.tsx:53-58,135-144`); the dialog "Edit expiration" `m:ov:edit-dialog` ("Update how long {featureName} remains available for {targetId}.", a datetime-local "Expiration" and a checkbox "Keep active without an expiration", actions "Cancel" and contained "Save changes" / "Saving…") — `ListAllFeatures.tsx:234-268`. No control removes a flag.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: the cards and the populated grid.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: the DataGrid's loading overlay and a disabled "Refresh"; the Class select has no indicator (`ListAllFeatures.tsx:206,216`; `SystemWideFeatureFlags.tsx:13-24`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: the DataGrid library's own no-rows overlay; no custom text.
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: a red Alert above the grid with the message or "Unable to load feature flags."; add failures: an error snackbar with the message or "Unable to add the class feature flag." / "Unable to add the user feature flag."; an edit failure ("Unable to update the feature flag.") sets the same card Alert, which sits **behind the open dialog** (`ListAllFeatures.tsx:49,103-107,212`).
  - `m:success` Success `[S]`: the add snackbars; edit success is silent (the dialog closes and the grid reloads).

### A-07 · MCP server registry — `/admin/mcp-servers`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/MCPServerManagement.tsx:41` (route `src/App.tsx:152-155`, wrapped in `AdminProtectedRoute`); dialogs `src/components/MCP/MCPServerDialog.tsx`, `MCPTestResultDialog.tsx`, `DeleteConfirmDialog.tsx`; frame SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader`: `MCPServerManagement.tsx:39,280-303`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `AdminProtectedRoute`: no user → `/login`; consent missing → `/consent`; admin status unknown → a centred spinner; not admin and not instructor → `/`. It therefore **admits instructors** (D-1; `src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:15-42`). **Entry visibility:** sidebar "MCP Server Registry" is admin-only (`src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:86-91`); the chat-agent sitemap says admin (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:89-94`).
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none (the nearest reading surfaces are the tool-schema JSON and the error text in the test dialog; the rest is tool chrome).
- **Purpose:** An admin lists, creates, edits, deletes and connection-tests the global MCP servers; assigning a server to classes happens on A-22.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "MCP Server Registry"; **the return from an OAuth round trip** (below); the chat agent (`mcp-servers`); a typed URL. No other page links here.
- **OAuth round trip, as coded:** "Test Connection" on a server that needs OAuth and has no active user connection opens "Authorization Required" (`MCPServerManagement.tsx:139-153`); "Authorize" stores `sessionStorage["mcp_oauth_return"]` = `{"returnTo":"/admin/mcp-servers","action":"test","serverId":…}` and sets `window.location.href` to the provider (`:187-202`); the backend callback redirects the browser to `{FRONTEND_URL}/?mcp_oauth_success=true` or `…/?mcp_oauth_error=<message>` (`../kiwi/src/mcp/mcp-user.controller.ts:109-153`); route `/` mounts `ProtectedRoute`, whose mount effect reads and deletes the key and navigates to `returnTo`, rendering nothing meanwhile (`src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:17-28,47-49`). `action` and `serverId` are never read, so the test does not re-run, and `mcp_oauth_success` / `mcp_oauth_error` are read nowhere in `src/`, so **no success or error message for the round trip is ever shown**.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "MCP Server Management"; description "Manage global MCP servers and assign them to classes from class settings."; actions: outlined "Refresh" (disabled while loading, no reason) and contained "Create Server" — `MCPServerManagement.tsx:280-300`.
  2. List region, exactly one of: *loading* — a table with the real header cells and three skeleton rows (`:305-331`); *empty* — `h6` "No MCP Servers Configured", "Create a global MCP server, then assign it to classes from the class MCP settings page." and a contained "Create Your First Server" (`:332-354`); *loaded* — a table with columns "Name" (name and description caption), "Transport" (chip HTTP / SSE), "Status" (chip "Active" / "Inactive"), "Assigned Classes" (chip "{n} classes", always plural), "OAuth" (chip "Required" or outlined "No"), "Actions" (icon buttons with tooltips "Test Connection", "Edit", "Delete" in error colour) (`:356-445`). No search, sort, pagination or row click.
  3. Overlay `m:ov:server-dialog`, Add/Edit dialog (md): title "Add MCP Server" / "Edit MCP Server"; "Basic Information" ("Server Name", "Description"); "Transport Protocol" ("HTTP" "Standard HTTP connection", "SSE" "Server-Sent Events"); "Connection Settings" ("Server URL", "Headers (optional)" with "Header Name", "Value", "Add Header"); a clickable row with the switch "Requires OAuth Authentication" and a chip "OAuth 2.1" that expands "Auto-Discover", "Auto-Register Client", "Authorization URL", "Token URL", "Client ID", "Client Secret", "Scopes", "Redirect URI" and a caption "Configure OAuth 2.1 settings for user authentication with this MCP server. Client secrets are stored securely and will not be displayed after saving."; a status switch "Server is Active" / "Server is Inactive" with "Inactive servers will not be available for use"; actions "Cancel", "Create" / "Update" / "Saving..." — `MCPServerDialog.tsx:441-817`. Inline validation is helper text on submit ("Name is required", "URL is required", "URL must start with http:// or https://", "Authorization URL is required", "Token URL is required", "Client ID is required", "Client Secret is required"); the OAuth errors sit inside the collapsible block and a failed submit does not expand it. The optional class selector in the dialog is never shown by this page.
  4. Overlay `m:ov:test-dialog`, "Connection Test Result" (md): "Testing connection to MCP server...", "Connection Successful" + "Found {n} available tool{s}", "Connection Failed" + the error or "Unknown error occurred", "Available Tools" with each tool's name and description or "No description" and an expandable "Input Schema" JSON, "No tools were returned by the MCP server.", "Error Details", "No test results available", "Close" — `MCPTestResultDialog.tsx`.
  5. Overlay `m:ov:delete-dialog`, "Delete MCP Server": `Are you sure you want to delete "{name}"?` plus, when assigned, " This server is currently assigned to {n} class{es}. Deleting it will remove it from all classes." and " This action cannot be undone."; actions "Cancel", a contained red "Delete" — `MCPServerManagement.tsx:266-275,466-476`; `DeleteConfirmDialog.tsx:36-47`.
  6. Overlay `m:ov:authorize-dialog`, "Authorization Required": `The MCP server "{name}" requires OAuth authentication. You need to authorize your account before testing the connection.`; actions "Cancel", contained "Authorize" ("Redirecting...") — `:479-513`.
  7. Overlay `m:success` `m:error`, snackbar, bottom right, 5,000 ms — `:516-529`. Tooltips.

  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: header, actions, table.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: the skeleton table (every "Refresh" returns to it); the route guard's spinner; the OAuth pre-flight request before a test shows no indicator (`:76,143,305`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: the empty block, **which also shows after a failed first load** because the list stays empty (`:332-354`).
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: snackbars "Failed to load MCP servers", "Failed to delete MCP server" (the dialog closes anyway), "Failed to save MCP server" (the dialog stays, no detail), "Failed to start authorization"; a test failure opens the result dialog with "Failed to test server connection" or the backend text; the native `alert()` on 403 and 404; OAuth return errors are never shown (`:81,127,205,245`).
  - `m:success` Success `[S]`: snackbars "MCP server deleted successfully", "MCP server updated successfully", "MCP server created successfully" (`:124,231,239`).

### A-08 · App registry — `/admin/kiwi-apps`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/KiwiAppsAdmin.tsx:95` (route `src/App.tsx:156-159`, wrapped in `AdminProtectedRoute`); frame SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader` with title and description only: `KiwiAppsAdmin.tsx:568-572`); all other UI is inline MUI.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `AdminProtectedRoute`, which admits instructors too (D-1; `src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:40`). **Entry visibility:** sidebar "App Registry" is admin-only (`src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:92-97`); the chat-agent sitemap says admin.
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none (tables, chips, dialogs; the long strings are the UI URL and the system prompt, each cut to one line with the full text in a tooltip).
- **Purpose:** Lets a system admin whitelist app slugs (issuing a one-time registration secret) and review, inspect and unregister the Kiwi Apps that have self-registered, including approving or revoking each app's LLM prompts.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "App Registry"; the chat agent (`kiwi-apps`); a typed URL. No other page links here.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "Kiwi Apps Management"; description "Manage the app whitelist and registered Kiwi Apps. Apps must be whitelisted before they can self-register." — `KiwiAppsAdmin.tsx:569-572`.
  2. Tabs "Whitelist" (default) · "Registered Apps"; local state, both lists fetched on mount — `:574-579`.
  3. Whitelist toolbar: outlined "Refresh", contained "Add to Whitelist" — `:583-601`. Table columns "Slug", "Base URL", "Description", "Status", "Created", "Actions"; the slug in monospace; a status chip "Approved" (success, check icon), "Pending" (warning), "Rejected" (error) or the raw value; **Created is `new Date(date).toLocaleString()` with no locale passed**, or "Never"; row actions: icon buttons with tooltips "Edit" and a red "Remove" — `:656-723,526-565`.
  4. Registered Apps `m:loaded:registered` toolbar: only an outlined "Refresh". Table columns (expander), "Name", "Slug", "Category" (a chip with the raw category), "Version", "Status" ("Active" / "Inactive"), "Last Seen", "Actions" (a red trash with tooltip "Unregister") — `:735-878`. An expandable row holds three sections: "Registered UIs" (a nested table "UI Slug", "Name", "URL", "Placement", "Allowed Roles", "Order", "Status" "Enabled" / "Disabled"; "Loading UIs...", "No UIs registered for this app."), "App Scopes" ("Maximum Allowed Scopes (from whitelist)", "Prompt Scopes (from registered prompts)", "Max scopes define what this app can request. Enable/disable specific scopes per class in class settings." with no link) and "LLM Prompts" (a table with "Name", "Prompt ID", "System Prompt", "Settings", "Status" "Approved" / "Revoked" / "Pending", and a text "Revoke" or a contained green "Approve"; "Approve prompts to allow the app to use them for LLM requests. Review the system prompt before approving.") — `:881-1252`.
  5. Overlay `m:ov:add-dialog`, "Add to Whitelist" (sm): "Enter the app details. A registration secret will be generated that the app must use to self-register."; fields "App Slug" (placeholder "e.g., codegen", helper "Lowercase identifier for the app"), "Registration Secret" (masked, prefilled with a generated 48-character secret, helper "Minimum 32 characters. Share this with the app developer.", tooltips "Show secret" / "Hide secret" / "Generate new secret"), "Base URL (optional)", "Description (optional)", select "Status" ("Approved", "Pending", "Rejected"); "Maximum Allowed Scopes" with its caption and an "Add" button; actions "Cancel", contained "Add" — `:1263-1408`.
  6. Overlay `m:ov:secret-dialog`, the secret dialog: a warning-coloured title "Save Your Registration Secret"; a warning Alert "This is the only time the registration secret will be shown. Copy it now and share it securely with the app developer."; copy tooltip "Copy to clipboard"; contained "I've Copied the Secret" — `:1411-1483`.
  7. Overlay `m:ov:edit-dialog`, "Edit Whitelist Entry" (the slug disabled; an info Alert "The registration secret cannot be viewed or changed. To issue a new secret, delete this entry and create a new one."); "Remove from Whitelist" `m:ov:remove-dialog`: `Are you sure you want to remove "{slug}" from the whitelist? This will prevent the app from re-registering and invalidate its registration secret.` with a contained red "Remove"; **a native browser `confirm()`** `m:native:unregister-confirm` for unregister: `Are you sure you want to unregister the app "{slug}"?` — `:1486-1637,469`.
  8. Overlay `m:success` `m:error`, snackbar, bottom right, 5,000 ms — `:1640-1653`.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded:whitelist` Default `[T]` (about 960 px): tabs "Whitelist" · "Registered Apps"; a table with a monospace Base URL, a green "Approved" chip, a locale-formatted Created date, a purple edit icon and a red delete icon; **the Slug column is so narrow that "ics-r-lab" breaks onto three lines**.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: real column headers and three skeleton rows; "Refresh" swaps the table back to skeletons; per-section text in the detail row (`:603-629,746-776`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: "No Apps Whitelisted" with "Add an app slug to the whitelist to allow it to self-register." and a contained "Add First Whitelist Entry"; "No Apps Registered" with "Apps will appear here once they self-register. Make sure the app is whitelisted first." and no button (`:630-652,777-789`).
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: snackbars only, recovery by "Refresh": "Failed to load whitelist", "Failed to load registered apps", "Failed to load UIs for {slug}", "Failed to approve prompt", "Failed to revoke prompt", "Failed to copy secret", "Failed to save whitelist entry", "Failed to remove from whitelist", "Failed to unregister app"; after a failed list load the empty-state text is what remains; scope and prompt failures are console-only (`:167,183,200-225,248,268,296,333,442,460,479`).
  - `m:success` Success `[S]`: snackbars "Prompt approved", "Prompt revoked", "Whitelist entry updated", "Removed from whitelist", "App unregistered", "App added to whitelist successfully", and an info one "Secret copied to clipboard".
  - Page-specific `[S]`: validation snackbars "Slug is required" and "Registration secret must be at least 32 characters" (the Add button is already disabled until both hold); Approve and Revoke show a spinner while processing; the detail data is cached after the first load, a failed load included; three status vocabularies on one page: whitelist "Approved / Pending / Rejected", app "Active / Inactive", UI "Enabled / Disabled", prompt "Approved / Revoked / Pending".
- **Primary CTA:** "Add to Whitelist" → the Add dialog (`:593-599`). Other filled: "Add First Whitelist Entry" (empty state), per-prompt "Approve", the dialog buttons "Add", "I've Copied the Secret", "Save", and the red "Remove".
- **Exit / next:** none; the helper text mentions "class settings" with no link to A-23.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** status chips (four vocabularies, colour only for some); the narrow Slug column and table minimum widths (Phase 3); the native `confirm()`; the secret dialog (a consequence-first message already present); the date format.
- **Data surfaces (Phase 6, DW-6.5):** four Phase 3 tables. The allowlist, block 3: the identifier (monospace, one line at `--size-col-min-text` with the full text on hover and focus; the three-line break of the tour goes), Base URL (monospace, truncating the same way), Description (the wrap column, two lines, the full text on hover and focus), Status (a status chip with its icon), Created (`17 Oct 2026, 14:05`, `--size-col-min-date`, or the em dash named "No value" in place of "Never"), Actions. The registered apps, block 4: Name and the identifier (truncating), Category (a chip from the lookup), Version (left-aligned monospace: a version string is an identifier, not a quantity), Status (chip + icon), Last seen (`--size-col-min-date`), Actions; its nested tables: Registered UIs (UI identifier and Name truncating, URL monospace truncating, Placement and Allowed roles as chips, Order a right-aligned tabular integer at `--size-col-min-num`, Status a chip + icon) and LLM prompts (Name, Prompt ID monospace truncating, the instructions as the wrap column with the full text on hover and focus, Settings, Status, the row action).

### A-09 · Webhooks — `/admin/webhooks`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/WebhookManagement.tsx:87` (route `src/App.tsx:150`). Frame from SR-4: `AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader`, `AdminFormSurface` (`WebhookManagement.tsx:555-556,611,641`). Everything else is inline MUI in a 1,482-line file; no colour literals (colour comes from palette keys).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (`src/App.tsx:129-135,150`), so any signed-in user reaches it (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** the sidebar entry "Webhooks" is shown to admins only (`src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:98-103`, filter `:280-282`); the chat-agent sitemap lists it for admins (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:83-88`). Backend, for information only: create and list sit behind `ProfGuard`, update, delete and test behind `AdminGuard` (`../kiwi/src/webhooks/webhooks.controller.ts:59,73,232,252,471`).
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none (the page has no reading surface; the data table, tabs, pagination and monospace secret fields are tool chrome).
- **Purpose:** An admin creates, edits, deletes and test-fires webhook endpoints, manages each endpoint's API token and opens its delivery history, all from one table.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "Webhooks" (`AdminLayout.tsx:98-103`); button "Event Approvals" is the reverse link from A-10 only in the other direction (A-10 has none); a typed URL; the Kiwi chat agent's navigation tool (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:83-88`). No email or in-page link leads here (repo-wide search).
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "Webhook Management"; description "Create endpoints and monitor webhook delivery."; actions: icon button (tooltip "Refresh", aria-label "Refresh webhooks"), outlined warning button "Event Approvals" inside a warning-colour Badge showing the pending count, contained primary "Create Webhook" — `WebhookManagement.tsx:556-593`.
  2. Summary cards (`aria-label="Webhook summary"`): "Total webhooks", "Active", "Inactive", each an `h4` number from the unfiltered list; one column on phones, three from `sm`, max width 992 — `:595-639`.
  3. Tab strip "All" · "Active" · "Inactive" (no counts) inside the same outlined surface as the table; each tab shows the same table filtered by `isActive` — `:641-660`.
  4. Table, columns "Status", "Webhook ID", "URL", "Secret", "API Token", "Events", "Stats", "Actions" (`:1198-1209`). Per row: status chip "active" / "inactive" with icon and colour (`:1213-1226`); the full id as plain text, no copy control (`:1227`); URL `{basePath}{webhook.url}` in monospace truncated at 300 px with a native `title`, plus an icon-only copy button (`:1228-1258`); Secret as a read-only field of 20 "•" with eye and copy icon buttons and an info icon whose tooltip reads "Webhook secrets are used for HMAC signature validation to verify that webhook payloads are authentic" (`:1259-1299`); API Token as one of three shapes: a small outlined "Create Token" button, or a token-name chip (success colour when active) with tooltips "Regenerate token (old token will be invalidated)" and "Delete token" and a caption "Last used: {date}", or a warning Alert "New Token Created - Copy Now!" with a masked field and "⚠️ This token will not be shown again!" (`:1304-1405`); Events as ids joined by ", " or "All events" (`:1409-1413`); Stats "Deliveries: {n}" or "No deliveries yet" (`:1414-1428`); four icon buttons with tooltips "Delivery History", "Test", "Edit", "Delete" (`:1429-1463`).
  5. Pagination: MUI `TablePagination` with default labels, 10 rows, client-side (`:1469-1476`).
  6. Overlay `m:ov:create-dialog`, Create dialog: title "Create New Webhook"; warning Alert "Note: Webhook creation may fail due to a backend configuration issue. The webhook service needs to be updated to properly associate webhooks with authenticated users."; field "Events (comma-separated, * for all)" pre-filled "*", helper "Enter event names separated by commas, or * for all events"; actions "Cancel", "Create" — `:663-698`.

  - `m:loaded` Default (loaded) `[S]`: blocks 1-5 with rows (`:554-661,1194-1478`).
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: a centred spinner replaces the table region (`:1166-1172`); no skeleton; the cards read 0 until data returns (`:90,94`).

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/WebhookEventApprovals.tsx:95` (route `src/App.tsx:151`). Frame from SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader`, `AdminFormSurface`: `WebhookEventApprovals.tsx:545-546,591,633,667`). Tables, dialogs and chips are inline MUI; no colour literals.
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. - **Purpose:** An admin approves or rejects pending webhook events, one by one or in bulk, and reviews a 30-day audit trail of those decisions.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "Webhook Approvals" (`AdminLayout.tsx:104-109`); button "Event Approvals" with a pending-count badge on A-09 (`WebhookManagement.tsx:573-582`); a typed URL. No email or redirect.

### A-11 · User management — `/admin/user-management`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/UserManagement.tsx:101` (route `src/App.tsx:162`); all other JSX is inline in the 1,889-line file. SR-4 helpers: `AdminPage maxWidth="xl"` (`UserManagement.tsx:933`), `AdminPageHeader` (`:934-959`), `AdminFormSurface` (`:1341`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. Today D-8 (a record-only defect row in the matrix). **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** sidebar "User Management" is admin-only (`src/pages/admin/AdminLayout.tsx:56-61`); the chat-agent sitemap lists it for admins (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:101-106`).
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none (tool chrome: toolbar, filter pills, table, pagination, results table; the only prose is one-sentence helper text).
- **Purpose:** One admin workspace to see every account (signed up or only whitelisted), switch its access on or off, change its system role, reset a password-account's password, bulk-add emails or password accounts, and assign instructors to classes.
- **Entry points:** sidebar "User Management"; the chat agent's navigation destination `user-management`; a typed URL. No other page links here.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "User management"; description "Control account access, system roles, registrations, and instructor assignments from one workspace."; actions: outlined "Assign instructor" and contained "Add users" — `UserManagement.tsx:934-959`.
  2. Toolbar: a static label "Table" with a table icon (aria-label "Current view: Table"; it is not a control and no second view exists); search field, placeholder "Search" (aria-label "Search accounts", matches email only); outlined "Export CSV", disabled when no rows match, no reason shown, which downloads `whitelist_{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv` with header "Email,Status,Operation Status,Error" — `:1363-1410,707-724`.
  3. Filter row (aria-label "Account filters"): three pill-shaped selects with leading icons — Access ("All access", "Enabled", "Disabled"), Role ("All roles", "User", "Instructor", "Admin"), Account status ("All statuses", "Registered", "Pending signup") — and a text button "Clear filters" that appears only while a search or filter is active — `:1426-1501`.
  4. List region: the loading branch, the empty branch, or the table (from `lg`, 1200 px) / the cards (below `lg`) — `:1503-1526`, `:1529`, `:1754`.
  5. Table (aria-label "User accounts", fixed layout): columns "Account" (sortable, 32%), "Access" (sortable), "Role", "Account status", "Account action". Row: bold email with caption "OAuth" or "Password"; a small green switch (aria-label "Enable access for {email}" / "Disable access for {email}") with the text "Enabled" / "Disabled"; a borderless role select ("User", "Admin", "Instructor") tinted warning for admin and info for instructor; a bordered status box with a 7 px dot and "Pending" / "Registered"; the action cell reading italic "Awaiting Registration", an outlined "Reset password" (password accounts) or italic "Managed by OAuth" — `:1545-1747`. Under the table sort headers; there is no sort control in the card layout, although the sort state applies to both.
  6. Cards (below `lg`): bold email; an outlined chip "OAuth" / "Password" and a filled chip "Pending" (warning) / "Registered" (success); the switch with the caption "Enabled" / "Disabled"; a labelled "Role" select; the action as caption "Awaiting registration" or "Password managed by OAuth" or the outlined "Reset password" — `:1755-1857`.
  7. Pagination: MUI `TablePagination` (5, 10, 25, 50; default 10; MUI default strings), hidden when there are no rows — `:1859-1875`.
  8. Overlay `m:ov:add-dialog`, Dialog "Add users" (md): subtitle "Choose whether to grant access or create password-based accounts."; tabs "Whitelist access" · "Password accounts". Whitelist tab: `h3` "Grant product access", text "Existing accounts are enabled immediately. Password tab: `h3` "Create password accounts", text "Use this only for non-SSO users.   9. Overlay `m:ov:instructors-dialog`, Dialog "Instructor assignments" (md): subtitle "Assign an instructor to a class or update an existing assignment."; selects "Class" and "Instructor", a multi-select "Permissions" ("Manage Materials", "View Analytics"); an info Alert "{selectedInstructor} is already assigned to this class. It stays open after success.

- **States:**

### A-12 · Admin app view (host frame) — `/admin/app/:appSlug`, `/admin/app/:appSlug/class/:classId`, `/admin/class/:classID/app/:appSlug`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/AdminAppPage.tsx:28` (routes `src/App.tsx:160,161,183`, none wrapped in `AdminProtectedRoute`) rendering `AdminAppView` (`src/pages/admin/AdminAppView.tsx:42`); `src/apps/adminNavigation.ts`, `src/context/AdminNavigationContext.tsx`. No SR-4 helper is used: the frame is full-bleed. **Only the host frame is specified; the embedded app's content is out of scope.**
- **Roles (Appendix A):** I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** an admin-panel UI appears in the sidebar only for roles in its `allowedRoles` (`AdminLayout.tsx:222-269,476-487`); an instructor on the classless route is redirected to their first assigned class's scoped route or `/admin/classes` (`AdminLayout.tsx:384-408`).
- **Density:** compact (the host chrome); the embedded app sets its own. · **Paper surfaces:** the Kiwi App iframe (`AdminAppView.tsx:563-580`): the embedded document stays light in dark mode (G5); the host frame and veil follow the mode. **Never recoloured:** everything inside the iframe. · **Density overrides:** none drawn by the host.
- **The three routes:** route 1 `/admin/app/:appSlug` is the global scope (no class, no enablement check, no `classId` in the iframe URL; a token is requested with an empty body, issued to system admins only); route 2 `/admin/app/:appSlug/class/:classId` is the class scope and the URL shape the host itself generates; route 3 `/admin/class/:classID/app/:appSlug` is a legacy shape that no sidebar item or switcher produces and that mounts the admin class wrapper. Routes 2 and 3 behave the same in page code. Changing the class re-runs the lookup (`AdminAppPage.tsx:32-36,42-51`; `AdminAppView.tsx:78-79,91-122,192-194`; `src/apps/adminNavigation.ts:54-60,80-85`).
- **Purpose:** Looks up the app's admin-panel UI by slug and hosts it in a full-height iframe, handing it the user and class context and an app token over `postMessage`.
- **Entry points:** the sidebar item named after the app (the UI name or the app name, with an apps icon); the top-bar class switcher on an app route (`AdminLayout.tsx:413-426`); the instructor redirect; the chat agent; bookmarks.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. The shell, with the app's item selected and, if the app sends `kiwi:adminNavigation`, validated child items under it (at most 20, label up to 80 characters, internal paths only) (`AdminLayout.tsx:476-487`; `AdminAppView.tsx:353-376`; `adminNavigation.ts:87-152`).
  2. Lookup: a centred spinner with "Loading admin panel..." (`AdminAppPage.tsx:92-110`).
  3. Lookup error: a centred red Alert with the text or "Admin panel not found": "Missing app slug", `App "{appSlug}" does not have an admin panel`, "Failed to load app admin panel"; no retry (`:112-127,45,79,83`).
  4. "Not enabled" panel `m:not-enabled` (class routes only, when the class lacks the app): an apps-icon tile, the heading "Exercise Manager is not enabled for this class", the text "Enable the Codegen app in this class before opening its exercise management tools.", and for system admins a contained "Manage Class Apps" (to A-23) or for others an info Alert "Ask an administrator to enable Codegen for this class." — `AdminAppView.tsx:405-489`. The names are hard-coded although the host renders any app.
  5. Iframe-load error: a centred red Alert "Failed to load {appName}" with a refresh icon button (aria-label "Retry loading {appName}") — `AdminAppView.tsx:491-519`.
  6. Default frame: a borderless `Paper` (elevation 0, full size) holding a loading veil (`background.paper`, spinner and "Loading {appName}...") over the iframe. The iframe is mounted only once the user id, role context and class enablement are resolved, has `title={appName}`, `border: none`, `display: none` until `load`, no host-set background, no `allow` attribute, and the sandbox "allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox allow-downloads"; its `src` is the UI URL plus `appId`, `userId`, `placement=admin-panel`, `classId` (class scope) and `uiSlug` — `AdminAppView.tsx:521-581,186-199`. **No toolbar, title bar, breadcrumb or status label surrounds it.**
  7. Bridge handshake (no visible status): on `kiwi:ready` the host sends `kiwi:context` and `kiwi:appToken`; `kiwi:requestToken` gets a new token; a token failure is sent to the app, not drawn (`AdminAppView.tsx:288-346`).
  8. No overlay owned by the page. The Kiwi Chat launcher (SR-6) overlays the frame.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: the iframe fills the main area under the top bar.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: two sequential indicators ("Loading admin panel...", then the veil "Loading {appName}..."); the veil also covers the time the iframe is unmounted and has no timeout if the user id never resolves (derived; `AdminAppView.tsx:126-138,562`).
  - `m:none` Empty: none; the nearest are the lookup errors and the "not enabled" panel.
  - `m:error:lookup` `m:error:iframe` Error `[S]`: blocks 3 and 5, fixed English strings (the real error is logged only); a failed class-enablement check does not block, the frame loads (`:108-114`).
  - `m:none` Success: none.
  - Page-specific `[S]`: a `class-admin-panel` UI is accepted when no `admin-panel` UI exists (`AdminAppPage.tsx:65-74`), while the host always sends `placement: 'admin-panel'` (`AdminAppView.tsx:191,333`).
- **Primary CTA:** none in the default frame (the host draws no buttons); in the "not enabled" panel "Manage Class Apps" → `/admin/class/{classId}/kiwi-apps` (`AdminAppView.tsx:469-478`).
- **Exit / next:** "Manage Class Apps" → A-23; app-supplied sidebar items navigate inside the iframe through `kiwi:adminNavigate`; otherwise the sidebar and class switcher.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** the veil and error Alerts (empty-state frame, loading); the paper boundary around the iframe; the sandbox is unchanged.

"Exercise Manager" and "Codegen" were hard-coded although the host renders any app, so the revised panel takes the app's name.

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/ClassSpecificFeatureFlags.tsx:10` (route `src/App.tsx:173`); `AddClassFeature.tsx` (with `hideClassSelection`), `ListClassFeatures.tsx`; frame SR-4 (`AdminPage maxWidth="xl"`, `AdminPageHeader`: `:53-57`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. - **Content blocks (in order):**

Active lectures — value `{active}` with the third line "Of 12 lectures in the class" (the ratio's denominator is its baseline; today's `3/12` goes, rows P6-A-18); with a lecture chosen the tile is Last activity — the date (A-18.04) and "No earlier period to compare". **Student intent (DW-6.2, DW-6.4, DW-6.6), block 6:** the 12 px stacked bar of seven hues becomes a horizontal bar chart of the intents sorted by count, "Other" last: one series in `--chart-1`, each row labelled with the intent's name, the bar from a `--chart-baseline` zero line (at most 24 px thick, a 4 px radius at the data end, a 2 px gap; no vertical gridlines, so nothing runs through the labels), the share as a direct label at the bar's end (`{share}%`), so the bar's length is its share, and no value axis (the labels are the values, as on Top actions; the counts are in the cards below and the summary), a scope line under the helper ("Questions by intent, all time"; "Questions by intent in this lecture, all time", rows P6-A-18: the page has no date range), the figure's caption a text summary (an unscoped and a lecture-scoped reading), the figure named by its title and described by its caption; each bar is a real button with a name and a tab stop (SF-29), drawn in HTML so that nothing focusable sits inside a hidden SVG, its tooltip the count its share stands for (`{n: count question}`, P6-A-18.07), hover `--surface-hover`, focus the ring; the cards below keep their words and drop the colour squares. - **Copy (Phase 6):** 18 strings added or revised (rules C3, C4, C16); every row is in the [Revision index](#revision-index) under [Rows appended by later phases](#rows-appended-by-later-phases). Phase 6 (kiwi-ui/DESIGN.md § Chart tokens): the KPI tiles' third line (the Questions tile's week-on-week trend, one row per direction, the denominator where the value is a ratio, or that there is no earlier period), the intent chart's direct label (its share: the chart draws no value axis) and its bars' tooltip (the count), and the text summaries of the intent chart and the topic bars, each in its unscoped and its lecture-scoped reading. The four scope lines state what each chart covers, because the page has no date range.
  - `P6-A-18.01` (none) → `Last full week: {m: count question}, up from {previous} the week before` · C4, C3 · The Questions tile's third line (`§ Chart tokens › KPI tiles`): a week-on-week trend from the weekly series the page already fetches and never draws (`weeklyActivity`, classAnalyticsApi.ts:20), so the tile carries a trend and not just context. This reading shows when the last full week had more questions than the week before (`{m}` > `{previous}`); the other directions are P6-A-18.17 (down) and P6-A-18.18 (the same). The weeks are the backend's UTC Mondays (`date_trunc('week')` over the class's chat questions, ../kiwi/src/analytics/class-analytics.service.ts:177-183, sent as the UTC instant of Monday 00:00 by `toISOString()`): the last full week is the latest Monday-to-Sunday week that has ended in UTC, and the week before is the Monday seven days earlier; a week missing from the series counts as 0, because the GROUP BY returns no row for a week without questions. The comparison is drawn only when the week before falls on or after the series' first week; otherwise, with an empty series, and while a lecture is chosen (the value is then that lecture's count and the series the whole class's), the line is "No earlier period to compare" (the tile rows below). The line takes the Phase 3 tile's direction glyph in its own colour (`--kpi-tile-trend`), hidden from assistive technology: the words state the direction, so neither the glyph nor a colour carries it. No percentage: a change between small counts reads larger than it is, and a week from 0 has none. (C4, C3: Redish; Nielsen #4)
  - `P6-A-18.02` (none) → `No earlier period to compare` · C16 · The Active students tile's third line: the class analytics API returns totals only, so no earlier period exists to compare and the line says so (C16). (C16: G12; ai-native: calibrate)

  - `P6-A-18.06` (none) → `Of {total: count lecture} in the class` · C4 · The Active lectures tile's third line: the denominator of the ratio the value used to draw (`§ Chart tokens › KPI tiles`), with the noun written by the helper (C4). (C4: Redish; Nielsen #4)
  - `P6-A-18.07` `${intent.label} · ${intent.questionCount} (${Math.round(share)}%)` → `{n: count question}` · C4 · Each intent bar's tooltip, on hover and on focus (IntentsPanel.tsx:80): the count its share stands for, with its unit by the helper ("71 questions"). ### A-20 · Experiment form — `/admin/class/:classID/experiments/new` and `/admin/class/:classID/experiments/:experimentId/edit`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/experiments/ExperimentForm.tsx:161` (one component for both routes, `src/App.tsx:178-179`); shared `src/pages/admin/experiments/experimentUi.tsx`; only `AdminPageHeader` of SR-4 is used (through `PageHeader`, `experimentUi.tsx:103-118`). The page sits inside `ExperimentTheme`, a local theme that gives buttons and inputs a 14 px radius (`experimentUi.tsx:15-30`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** the class sub-menu item "Experiments" has no instructor restriction (`src/pages/admin/ClassLayout.tsx:44`) and stays selected on this route; it leads to the list, not here. Backend, for information: `InstructorClassGuard` (`../kiwi/src/experiment/experiment.controller.ts:51`).
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** the system-prompt textareas and the student-email chip lists hold long prose and lists (reading-like); the Σ chip, accordions, sticky action bar and import/export card are tool chrome.
- **Purpose:** One form with two modes: an admin or instructor defines (create) or changes (edit) a per-class chat A/B experiment (name, how students are split into variant groups, each variant's chat engine and system prompt) and saves it as a draft or saves and activates it.
- **Entry points:** *create* — button "New Experiment" on A-19 (`ExperimentList.tsx:74-87`), empty-list button "Create your first experiment" (`:134-141`), the Experiment Assistant (SR-7) when a reply carries a config (`ExperimentAssistant.tsx:221-228`), the Kiwi chat agent (`src/agent/sitemap.ts:156-166`), a typed URL. *edit* — row button "Edit" on A-19 (`ExperimentList.tsx:209-217`), button "Edit" on A-21 (`ExperimentDetail.tsx:215-222`), a typed URL.
- **Content blocks (in order):** one scrolling column, max width 900, of four section cards plus a sticky action card; no stepper, tabs or wizard (`ExperimentForm.tsx:639-1239`).
  1. Page header: `h1` "New Experiment" or "Edit Experiment"; description "Design variant groups, then review and submit. The AI assistant can draft this for you." (create) / "Update groups, assignment, and prompts. Active experiments use saved changes on future chats." (edit); back button "Back to Experiments" — `:617-626`.
  2. Banner slot: a dismissible error Alert, then a dismissible info Alert — `:628-637`.
  3. Card "Basics": field "Experiment name"; multiline "Description" — `:640-659`.
  4. Card "Group Assignment": radio "Manual lists" ("Paste student emails for each group") and "Seeded split" ("Random split by your allocation %, exact counts. Same seed reproduces it; Reshuffle re-rolls."), the default being "Seeded split"; for seeded, field "Seed" with helper "The random seed. Keep it to reproduce the same split; edit it or click Reshuffle for a new one."; a warning Alert if the roster fails to load ("Couldn't load the class roster: {rosterError}. Group preview is unavailable until it loads."); subheading "Student groups" with text button "Reshuffle" (seeded) or "Recompute" (manual); then the preview, one outlined box per variant with a 4 px left border in a literal engine colour (`#6366f1` for qwen, `#10b981` for openai), an engine chip, a count chip ("{n} students · target {pct}%") and one chip per student email, or "No students" — `:661-868`.
  5. Card "Variants": header chip "{assigned} / {rosterCount} assigned" and text button "Random assign" (manual) or chip "Σ {sum}" that is green at 1.00 and red otherwise (seeded); no text says what the sum must be. One outlined panel per variant with fields "Key", "Label", "Allocation" (0-1, disabled in manual with helper "set by roster"), select "Engine" ("openai", "qwen") and a delete icon (aria-label "remove variant", disabled at two variants, no reason shown); in manual mode an accordion "Members — {n} student(s)" with a label-less textarea (placeholder "student emails, comma or newline separated") and red captions "Invalid email format (ignored): …" and "Not enrolled in this class (ignored): …"; an accordion "System prompt" with a chip "Customized" or "Using default", a text button "Reset" and a label-less textarea; then outlined "Add variant" — `:870-1139`.

Overlays `m:G-2`: none of MUI's (no Dialog, Snackbar, Tooltip, Popover); the engine select menu; the native file chooser; the native `alert()` for HTTP 403 and 404 from the shared middleware (`src/utils/middleware.ts:105-110`). - **Primary CTA:** "Submit (draft)" (create), "Submit & activate" (create, box checked), "Save" (edit), "Save & activate" (edit, box checked), "Submitting…" while busy → validate, create or update, optionally activate, then A-21 (`:579-601,1210-1221`). It is the only `variant="contained"` button, drawn on `violetGradient`, `linear-gradient(135deg, #6a1b9a 0%, #616161 100%)` (`experimentUi.tsx:35-37`).

### A-21 · Experiment detail — `/admin/class/:classID/experiments/:experimentId`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/experiments/ExperimentDetail.tsx:77` (route `src/App.tsx:180`); shared `experimentUi.tsx`, `grouping.ts`; SR-7; only `AdminPageHeader` of SR-4, through `PageHeader`. Centred column of at most 920 px inside `ExperimentTheme` (`ExperimentDetail.tsx:198-199`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** I, A. **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** the class sub-menu "Experiments" stays selected here but links to the list; the sitemap has no detail destination.
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** the prompt text boxes and the description paragraph are reading surfaces; accordions, chips, stat pills and the action row are tool chrome.
- **Purpose:** Shows one experiment's status, assignment strategy and, per variant, its engine, allocation, student and chat counts, student list and system prompt, and lets the instructor edit it, activate or re-activate it, turn it off or export its config as JSON.
- **Entry points:** a card on A-19 (`ExperimentList.tsx:149`); after submitting A-20 (`ExperimentForm.tsx:595`); the class switcher keeps the suffix, including the experiment id; a typed URL.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` the experiment name (no fallback for an empty name); description `{assignment label} · seed "{seed}" · by {unit}` (labels "Seeded split", "Random on first chat", "Manual lists"); a status chip; a back arrow (aria-label "Back to Experiments") — `ExperimentDetail.tsx:165-175,201-205`.
  2. A dismissible error Alert with the raw `{error}` — `:208-212`.
  3. Action row: outlined "Edit"; by status contained "Activate" (draft) or "Re-activate" (completed), or a red outlined "Turn off" (active); always outlined "Export JSON", which downloads `{name or "experiment"}.json` with member lists stripped — `:214-241,136-154`. **No delete control and no confirmation wording** for Activate, Re-activate or Turn off exist on this page.
  4. Description paragraph, only when set — `:243-251`.
  5. Overline "Variants · {n}" — `:253-260`.
  6. One card per variant, stacked with a staggered fade-in (the whole "variant comparison": no side-by-side view, chart or results panel): label, key (monospace), engine chip (raw id), allocation chip "{n}%"; two stat pills "students" and "chats"; an accordion "Students in this group" (collapsed; chip "{n} students" always plural; email chips or "No students"; absent for the random strategy); an accordion "System prompt" (collapsed; chip "Customized" or "Using default"; the prompt in a white bordered box or "(empty — class default applies)") — `:261-424`.
  7. SR-7, rendered only in the loaded state — `:426`. On this URL it starts as the launcher unless the user left it open on another experiment page.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: as above.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: a full-page violet spinner replaces everything (header, buttons and the assistant), on first load and after every Activate, Re-activate or Turn off (`:95,156-161`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: "No students" in a group; "(empty — class default applies)"; no description block; no empty state for zero variants (the heading would read "Variants · 0").
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: an unknown id or a failed first load shows an Alert "{error || "Not found"}" and nothing else, with no header, back button or retry (`:162-163`); later failures show the dismissible Alert above the actions. The counts, analytics, roster and defaults requests each swallow errors (`:96-102`), giving zero pills and "Using default" chips with no message.
  - `m:none` Success `[S]`: none; no snackbar; Export gives a browser download with no message.
  - Page-specific `[S]`: no busy state during Activate or Turn off (`:127-134,223-237`); an empty variant prompt with a non-empty class default is labelled "Customized" while its text reads "(empty — class default applies)" (derived from code).
- **Primary CTA:** "Activate" (draft) or "Re-activate" (completed) → `experimentApi.activate` then a reload (`:223-232`). For an active experiment there is no filled button; "Turn off" is outlined.
- **Exit / next:** back arrow → A-19 (`:205`); "Edit" → A-20 (`:218`); SR-7 → A-20 prefilled.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** status and engine chips; stat pills (a KPI-like element, Phase 3); the not-found Alert (empty-state frame).

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/ClassMCPSettings.tsx:75` (route `src/App.tsx:181`); `src/components/MCP/ToolConfigPanel.tsx` and the three dialogs shared with A-07; frame SR-4 (`ClassMCPSettings.tsx:52,445-449`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** A (admin-only). **Instructors (decision of 2026-10-16):** no access; an instructor who reaches the page should see a no-permission state, not be signed out and not be sent back with an `alert()`. - **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none (tool chrome).
- **Purpose:** An admin assigns global MCP servers to this class, switches them on or off for the class, creates or edits servers, and enables or disables the class's tools (built-in and MCP).

- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: tab "MCP Servers" with the table.

  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: as in block 3 and block 4.
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: snackbars "Failed to load MCP servers", "Failed to load global servers", "Failed to load tool configurations" (shown at page load even while on the first tab), "Failed to load server details", "Failed to unassign server", "Failed to save MCP server", "Failed to update server assignments", "Failed to update server status", "Failed to update tool configuration" (`:129,143,159,199,224,300,372,400,421`); a failed global-server fetch still opens the assign modal with stale content; a test failure shows "Failed to test server connection", and unlike A-07 there is no OAuth pre-check.

### A-23 · Class apps — `/admin/class/:classID/kiwi-apps`

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/ClassKiwiAppsSettings.tsx:53` (route `src/App.tsx:182`); frame SR-4 (`AdminPage`, `AdminPageHeader` with title, description and actions: `ClassKiwiAppsSettings.tsx:370-389`).
- **Roles (Appendix A):** I, A. **Instructors:** granted; today the class sub-menu hides the entry (D-4). **Guard (code):** `ProtectedRoute` only (B1, D-5). **Entry visibility:** the class sub-menu item "Class Apps" is hidden from instructors although Appendix A grants the page (D-4; `src/pages/admin/ClassLayout.tsx:40,154-155`); not in the sitemap. A "Class Apps" card in the unrouted `ClassManagement.tsx:153-158`.
- **Density:** compact · **Paper surfaces:** none · **Density overrides:** none.
- **Purpose:** Lets a system admin choose which registered Kiwi Apps appear as student tabs in one class, set their order and tab label, and restrict which of an app's scopes it may use in that class.
- **Entry points:** class sub-menu "Class Apps" (SR-3); the button "Manage Class Apps" on A-12's "not enabled" panel (`AdminAppView.tsx:468-480`); the class switcher keeps the sub-route; a typed URL.
- **Content blocks (in order):**
  1. Page header: `h1` "Kiwi Apps"; description "Manage which apps are available for students in this class."; actions: outlined "Refresh" and contained "Enable Apps" — `:371-389`.
  2. Enabled-apps table: columns "Order" (two arrow icon buttons per row, with no tooltip or label), "App" (name and slug), "Category" (a chip with the raw category), "Capabilities" (first three raw strings as outlined chips and a "+{n}" chip), "Tab Label" (the custom label or an italic grey "Default"), "Actions" (tooltips "Edit" and a red "Disable") — `:444-530`.
  3. Overlay `m:ov:enable-dialog`, "Enable Apps" (sm): "Loading available apps..." (no spinner), "No registered apps available. Apps must be registered in the system first.", or a checklist of all active registered apps (name, category chip, slug, up to three capability chips), already enabled ones pre-checked; actions "Cancel", contained "Save" — `:537-631`.
  4. Overlay `m:ov:edit-dialog`, "Edit App Settings": field "Tab Label" (placeholder the app name, helper "Custom label for the app tab. Leave empty to use the app's default name."); "Enabled Scopes" with "Loading scopes...", "No scopes defined for this app. The app's whitelist entry may not have any maxScopes configured." or "Select which scopes this app can use in this class. If none are selected, all max scopes are allowed." and one row per scope (a chip filled when on, an extra chip "from prompt", a small switch) and "Enabled: {n} of {m} scopes"; actions "Cancel", "Save" — `:634-751`.
  5. Overlay `m:ov:disable-dialog`, "Disable App": `Are you sure you want to disable "{name}" for this class? Students will no longer have access to this app.` with a contained red "Disable" ("Disabling...") — `:754-775`.
  6. Overlay `m:success` `m:error`, snackbar (success or error only), 5,000 ms — `:778-791`.
- **States:**
  - `m:loaded` Default `[S]`: the table.
  - `m:loading` Loading `[S]`: a two-row skeleton table; "Refresh" disabled (`:391-417`).
  - `m:empty` Empty `[S]`: "No Apps Enabled" with "Enable apps to give students access to additional tools and features in this class." and a contained "Enable Apps" (`:418-440`).
  - `m:error` Error `[S]`: snackbars "Failed to load enabled apps" (the list stays empty, so the empty state shows), "Failed to load available apps" (the dialog still opens, empty), "Failed to update app assignments", "Failed to update app", "Failed to disable app", "Failed to reorder apps"; a scope-load failure is console-only and shows the "No scopes defined" text (`:113,129,203,264,303,328,350,228-231`).
  - `m:success` Success `[S]`: "App assignments updated successfully", "App updated successfully", "App disabled successfully", "App order updated".
  - Page-specific `[S]`: each arrow click saves at once with no progress and no disabling; the Enable dialog's "Save" also **disables apps that were unchecked, with no confirmation**, one by one, so a mid-loop failure leaves a partial change (`:165-207,310-352`); with no scope explicitly selected all rows read "on", and flipping one makes it the only enabled scope (derived; `:271-279,687`).
- **Primary CTA:** "Enable Apps" (contained, header) → loads active registered apps and opens the dialog (`:384-386,140-146`). Also filled: the empty-state "Enable Apps", dialog "Save", the red "Disable".
- **Exit / next:** none; no link to the student tab or the registry.
- **Stage 1 hooks:** reorder arrows (unlabelled icon buttons); status and category chips; the empty-state frame.

- **Source:** `src/pages/admin/AnnotateDocument.tsx:198` (a 1,700-line file; routes `src/App.tsx:186-190`); `src/components/PDFViewer/PDFViewer.tsx`, `PdfSearch.tsx`, `src/components/ClickToSelect/ClickToSelect.tsx`, `src/components/DocumentSummaryDialog/DocumentSummaryDialog.tsx`; only `AdminPageHeader` of SR-4 (`AnnotateDocument.tsx:22,1401-1423`, no `AdminPage`). **The two routes do not differ**; only `/annotation` is linked from the UI. **Guard redirects** (behaviour of the wrappers, recorded for the matrix; none is a route):

- `ProtectedRoute`: signed out → `/login`; consent required and missing → `/consent`; a stored OAuth return context → its `returnTo`, or `/class/{classId}` (D-6) — `src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:17-58`.
- `UnprotectedRoute`: signed in → `/consent` if consent is missing, else `/admin` (instructor, admin) or `/` — `src/auth/UnprotectedRoute.tsx:15-26`.
- `AdminProtectedRoute`: signed out → `/login`; consent missing → `/consent`; admin status unknown → a centred spinner; neither admin nor instructor → `/` — `src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:15-42`.
- Page-level: `StudentClassLayout` replaces an unknown tab with the first tab, which is what makes R-5 (`src/pages/ClassLayout.tsx:192-207`); `AdminLayout` sends an instructor on the classless admin-app route to their first assigned class or `/admin/classes` (`AdminLayout.tsx:384-408`); A-03 sends non-admins to `/admin/classes` (`Analytics.tsx:245-247`); A-02 returns to `/admin/classes` on close (`AddNewClass.tsx:393-394`).

## Verification matrix

What later phases and the implementation verify against, per the brief's done-when 2 and G13: **route x role x state x mode x viewport**.

**One rule.** Roles follow the intended access model, Appendix A as the user updated it on 2026-10-16: student accounts cannot enter the teacher and admin interface (`/admin/*`), instructors and admins can enter the student interface, the system-level admin pages and Class feature flags and Class MCP settings are admin-only, and the instructors of a class may use Enrolment and Class email. **A role gets a verified row if and only if Appendix A grants it.** A role that today's guards let in but Appendix A does not grant gets a record-only defect row: a student on a `/admin/*` page (defect B1, recorded in [Students on `/admin/*`](#students-on-admin-b1), with no row) and an instructor on an admin-only page (defect D-8, a record-only row in the Page rows and a cell in [Instructors on admin-only pages](#instructors-on-admin-only-pages-d-8)). A defect row has no state, mode or viewport cells; today's outcome stays as evidence, and the intended outcome is a no-permission state, which does not exist today. Where today's guards refuse a role that Appendix A grants (the instructors of a class on A-16 and A-17, D-9), the row stays a verified row and its Today column records the refusal.

What today's guards do is recorded next to the model: every page was walked once per role in source (none was run), driven by the guards (the route wrapper, the layout's and the page's own redirects, the page's first-load requests and whether each passes through the session middleware, and the backend guards and inline checks behind each request). The result is the [Role outcomes](#role-outcomes) tables, one cell per page and role with its source anchors, the two defect sections, and a Today column on every page row. The Page rows' States column is **generated from the `m:<id>` tags in the [Page specs](#page-specs)** (each States bullet and each overlay item carries its id). All of it was re-checked against its sources when this file was written: every page x role cell has an outcome and exactly one row or defect record; every States bullet and overlay item has an id; every row's states come from ids; and the guard list of every request in the pass equals the guard decorators in the backend source. A later phase that adds or changes a state or a guard changes its id, its outcome cell and its row together. Display-menu preferences (theme, Kiwi animation) and the motion settings (`VITE_ENABLE_MASCOT_MOTION`, reduced motion) are not a matrix dimension; they are verified in Phases 4 and 7 against done-when 7 and 8.

### Dimensions

| Dimension | Values | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Route | the 40 leaf routes of `src/App.tsx`: 39 are pages, folded to 34 page entries (multi-route pages list every route), and `/logout` is a redirect-only leaf (R-3) | The two `<Navigate>` routes (R-1, R-2) are counted outside the 40 (46 router entries = 1 root + 3 layouts + 2 `<Navigate>` + 40 leaves). The five redirects have a row of their own (Redirect rows): R-1 to R-3 are redirect-only routes, R-4 is the conditional redirect of `/consent` (the route is page S-09 when a consent form is configured) and R-5 is the direct-load redirect of S-04. |
| Role | signed out; S; I; A | By the one rule: S, I and A on every student, auth and fallback route (signed out too on the auth and fallback pages); A on all 24 admin pages; I on the 12 admin pages that Appendix A grants it, as verified rows; I on the 12 admin-only pages as record-only defect rows; **no S row on any `/admin/*` page**. A row's Outcome is what the role gets by design (`renders`, `redirects to ...`, or `defect record: no-permission state expected`) with, in square brackets, the flags that name a discrepancy or a role-specific control: `D-1` the wrapper admits instructors although the page is admin-only, `D-2` the sign-in pages redirect a signed-in user, `D-3` `/authorize` has no wrapper, `D-4` the class sub-menu hides an entry that Appendix A grants the instructor, `D-7` the page turns the role away itself, `D-8` an instructor on an admin-only page is signed out or bounced instead of seeing a no-permission state, `D-9` the backend refuses the instructors of a class on Enrolment and Class email, "view-switch icon, SR-1" and "Experiment row, SR-6e" the two controls that instructors and admins have on the student pages. The **Today** column says what the guards do now where that differs (`renders, then B2`); `same` where it does not. Signed out is a row only for the auth and fallback pages; elsewhere it is a redirect to `/login` (G-4). |
| State | the ids in the page specs: `loaded`, `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `success`, `submitting`, named page states, `ov:` overlays, `native:` browser dialogs | The states the page spec defines, "where the page has them" (done-when 2), **for the role as the page is meant to work for it**: a verified row whose Today is B2 still lists the page's states, because the refusal is the defect and not the design. A redirect row and a defect record have no cells; their outcome is recorded. A state the spec marks absent ("none") is tagged `m:none` and has no row. States the demo data cannot show need a fixture or a stalled or failed request; the spec marks them `[S]`. |
| Mode | light, dark | Both for every verification row. A redirect row has a mode dimension only where it renders something of its own: R-3's bare word "Logout" takes the mode's colours; R-1, R-2, R-4 and R-5 render nothing. Dark ships behind `VITE_ENABLE_DARK_MODE` (G3). Paper surfaces stay light in dark mode (G5). |
| Viewport | 1280x800 and 1440x900 for **every** route; 390x844 for **student, auth and fallback routes** (S-01 to S-10) | Admin routes are desktop-only (G13). Layouts that appear below 1200 px (the A-11 card layout) fall outside the verification viewports. |

### Role outcomes

Each cell below is **today's outcome** for an intended page and role, a conclusion from source and not an observation: this pass ran nothing and started no backend, and the tour (which used an older backend) observed none of these cells. The only live observations of these cells are the coordinator's checks of 2026-10-16 with an admin account, marked `[L]`: the course list (S-01) with its view-switch icon, the Experiment toggle row on a student class page, and a typed app URL (R-5). For every page and role the pass read (1) the route wrapper in `src/App.tsx` and `src/auth/`, (2) the redirects in the layouts and in the page, (3) the page's first-load requests and the client each one uses (middleware or plain `fetch`, G-3), (4) the backend route's guards, taken from the controller decorators by script (250 of the 257 generated client operations matched a backend route; the 7 that did not are MCP transport and well-known metadata endpoints that no page calls; the direct `fetch()` calls were read by hand and are named by path), and the handler's or service's own role checks, and (5) what the page does with each answer. Three scripted checks back the cells: every request's guard list equals the decorators, every status agrees with the guard table below (or names the inline check that differs), and every anchor resolves to a real line. A blind second reading of the first-load requests and the outcome of the 16 pages where a missed request would change a result (A-01, A-02, A-03, A-12, A-13, A-14, A-18 to A-21, A-23, A-24 and S-01 to S-04) agreed on every role; for S-04 it also found that a direct load redirects, which is R-5.

**Roles (fixtures).**

| Role | Fixture |
|---|---|
| signed out | No `authToken` in `localStorage`, or no `user` in the auth context. |
| S | `systemRole` `user`; enrolled as a student in the class under test; no instructor assignment; no professor enrollment. |
| I | `systemRole` `instructor`; actively assigned to the class under test with `canManageMaterials` and `canViewAnalytics`; no professor enrollment (assigning an instructor creates none: `../kiwi/src/instructor-class/instructor-class.service.ts:14-62`). Whether an instructor or an admin is also enrolled as a student in the class (an admin who created a class is enrolled as its professor) decides S-01's `loaded` and the comment pins of S-02; a cell says so where that, a permission flag or the missing professor enrollment decides the result. |
| A | `systemRole` `admin`. |
| All signed-in roles | Have consented, or no consent form is configured. Otherwise every route behind a wrapper first redirects to `/consent` (`src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:55-58`, `src/auth/UnprotectedRoute.tsx:16-18`, `src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:19-22`). |

**Outcome classes.** `renders`: no first-load request is refused for the role and nothing redirects it. `B2`: a first-load request answers 401 through the session middleware, so the role sees the first frame and is then signed out. `alert`: a first-load request answers 403 or 404 and the browser shows a native `alert()`; the page stays. `redirect`: the front end sends the role elsewhere.

**Mechanisms that apply to every page.**

| Row | Mechanism | Where |
|---|---|---|
| G-1 | **B2.** A call that goes through the session middleware and answers 401 is retried once after a token refresh (`GET /auth/refresh-token`, open to every signed-in role); the retry's 401, or a refresh that fails, clears `authToken` and `authUser` and sets `window.location.href` to `/login?timeout=true`, which shows the session-expired banner (S-05). The page is left, whatever it showed. If the refresh call itself is refused, `refreshAuthToken` first sets `/login?sessionExpired=true`, which S-05 does not read; which address wins is a navigation race and is not settled from source. | `src/utils/middleware.ts:6-41,61-102`; `src/pages/Login.tsx:100-104` |
| G-2 | **alert.** A 403 or 404 raises the browser's own `alert()` ("You do not have permission to perform this action." / "The requested resource was not found."); the response is then returned to the caller as usual. The alert is drawn by the browser, so its check is the wording and the trigger, not contrast. | `src/utils/middleware.ts:104-110` |
| G-3 | **Scope.** Only calls made with a client that carries the middleware pass through it: the default `apiClient` and the email, audit, webhook, token, MCP, tool, kiwi-app, class-app and permission clients of `src/utils/api.ts`, and so `experimentApi`, apart from its edit-save `PUT`. Direct `fetch()` calls (the class-analytics reads, the student comment and summary reads, A-24's comment and summary reads), `apiClientWithoutMiddleWare` and the app-token bridge client do not, so a refusal there is silent: no refresh, no alert, no sign-out. A cell names such calls where they matter. | `src/utils/api.ts:22-42,44-53,63-64`; `src/utils/experimentApi.ts:106-135,193-194` |
| G-4 | **Signed out.** On every page behind `ProtectedRoute` or `AdminProtectedRoute` a visitor without a user is redirected to `/login`, so signed out is a row only for the auth and fallback pages. | `src/auth/ProtectedRoute.tsx:51-53`; `src/auth/AdminProtectedRoute.tsx:15-17` |

**What the pass shows for I and A on the 24 admin pages.**

| Role | Granted pages: renders | Granted pages: refused (B2) | Admin-only pages: B2 after the first frame | Admin-only pages: alert, then redirect | Admin-only pages: renders, the submit is refused (B2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | 10 (A-01, A-12, A-13, A-14, A-18, A-19, A-20, A-21, A-23, A-24) | 2 (A-16, A-17) | 10 (A-04, A-05, A-06, A-07, A-08, A-09, A-10, A-11, A-15, A-22) | 1 (A-03) | 1 (A-02) |
| A | 24 (all) | 0 | n/a | n/a | n/a |

- **Instructors on the 12 admin-only pages** are signed out on 10 of them after the first frame, bounced with an `alert()` on A-03, and let into a form whose submit signs them out on A-02, instead of seeing a no-permission state (D-8, register B4). On A-04, A-05, A-07 and A-08 the wrapper even lets them in (D-1).
- **The instructors of a class are refused on Enrolment and Class email** (A-16, A-17; D-9, register B5): `ProfGuard` needs a professor enrolment, and assigning an instructor creates none (SF-65). Their class sub-menu entries are hidden too, as is Class Apps (A-23, which renders for them): D-4.
- **The sidebar already shows an instructor only the entries they may use among the system pages.** The nine system entries other than Classes are admin-only (`AdminLayout.tsx:50-110`); no entry an instructor sees leads to an admin-only page, so they reach those pages by a typed URL or through the chat agent's sitemap, which lists `new-class` and `analytics` for instructors (SR-3).
- **Four guards answer 401, not 403.** `AdminGuard`, `ProfGuard`, `InstructorClassGuard` and `InstructorRoleGuard` end the session; only `AnalyticsAdminGuard`, `AnalyticsAccessGuard` and `MaterialManageGuard` answer 403 and show an `alert()`. B2 is therefore the usual outcome of a refusal and `alert` the rare one.
- **An instructor's permission flags decide three pages**: A-14 and A-24 need `canManageMaterials` and A-18 needs `canViewAnalytics`; without them the instructor gets the student's outcome of the guard section below.
- **Plain `fetch` calls refuse silently** (G-3): the comment and summary reads of S-02 for an unenrolled I or A (no pins, no banner), and A-18's analytics reads when a flag is missing (an inline error).
- **The student class shell opens for any role and any class** (SF-64): an instructor or admin who is not enrolled still gets S-02 to S-04. The one enrollment-sensitive request, `POST /document`, answers 404 with an `alert()` for an instructor without `canManageMaterials`.

### Students on `/admin/*` (B1)

This is the guard section for students. **Intended outcome.** A student account cannot enter the teacher and admin interface: every `/admin/*` URL should turn a student away, to `/`. **Today** the `/admin` layout route is wrapped in `ProtectedRoute` only (`src/App.tsx:129-135`), so a student reaches the admin shell and what happens next depends on the page; the four pages wrapped in `AdminProtectedRoute` already turn a student away (`src/App.tsx:140-159`). This is defect **B1**. It is outside the Stage 1 boundary (a guard and routing change, not a visual one), and its fix, a role guard on the `/admin` layout route, is tracked separately. The table records today's outcome per page with source anchors, from the same pass as the Role outcomes above. **These cells are not verification rows: no S row exists for any `/admin/*` page.** Phase 7 verifies the turn-away once B1 is fixed (Appendix D).

What a student sees today is not uniform. The session ends after the first frame (B2) on 12 pages, but 5 pages render in full (A-01, A-02, A-12, A-18, A-23; A-01 lists every class in the system, SF-64), 2 raise an `alert()` and stay (A-14, A-24), and 5 redirect (A-03, A-04, A-05, A-07, A-08; A-04, A-05, A-07 and A-08 at the route wrapper before the page mounts, A-03 from inside the page after two `alert()`s, and it sends the student on to A-01, which renders).
